kjv.36:8: And every wise hearted man among them that wrought the work of the tabernacle made ten curtains [of] fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet: [with] cherubims of cunning work made he them.
kjv.36:9: The length of one curtain [was] twenty and eight cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits: the curtains [were] all of one size.
kjv.36:10: And he coupled the five curtains one unto another: and [the other] five curtains he coupled one unto another.
kjv.36:11: And he made loops of blue on the edge of one curtain from the selvedge in the coupling: likewise he made in the uttermost side of [another] curtain, in the coupling of the second.
kjv.36:12: Fifty loops made he in one curtain, and fifty loops made he in the edge of the curtain which [was] in the coupling of the second: the loops held one [curtain] to another.
kjv.36:13: And he made fifty taches of gold, and coupled the curtains one unto another with the taches: so it became one tabernacle.
kjv.36:14: And he made curtains [of] goats' [hair] for the tent over the tabernacle: eleven curtains he made them.
kjv.36:15: The length of one curtain [was] thirty cubits, and four cubits [was] the breadth of one curtain: the eleven curtains [were] of one size.
kjv.36:16: And he coupled five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.
kjv.36:17: And he made fifty loops upon the uttermost edge of the curtain in the coupling, and fifty loops made he upon the edge of the curtain which coupleth the second.
kjv.36:18: And he made fifty taches [of] brass to couple the tent together, that it might be one.
kjv.36:19: And he made a covering for the tent [of] rams' skins dyed red, and a covering [of] badgers' skins above [that].
kjv.36:20: And he made boards for the tabernacle [of] shittim wood, standing up.
kjv.36:21: The length of a board [was] ten cubits, and the breadth of a board one cubit and a half.
kjv.36:22: One board had two tenons, equally distant one from another: thus did he make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
kjv.36:23: And he made boards for the tabernacle; twenty boards for the south side southward:
kjv.36:24: And forty sockets of silver he made under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for his two tenons, and two sockets under another board for his two tenons.
kjv.36:25: And for the other side of the tabernacle, [which is] toward the north corner, he made twenty boards,
kjv.36:26: And their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
kjv.36:27: And for the sides of the tabernacle westward he made six boards.
kjv.36:28: And two boards made he for the corners of the tabernacle in the two sides.
kjv.36:29: And they were coupled beneath, and coupled together at the head thereof, to one ring: thus he did to both of them in both the corners.
kjv.36:30: And there were eight boards; and their sockets [were] sixteen sockets of silver, under every board two sockets.
kjv.36:31: And he made bars of shittim wood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
kjv.36:32: And five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the sides westward.
kjv.36:33: And he made the middle bar to shoot through the boards from the one end to the other.
kjv.36:34: And he overlaid the boards with gold, and made their rings [of] gold [to be] places for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
kjv.36:35: And he made a vail [of] blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen: [with] cherubims made he it of cunning work.
kjv.36:36: And he made thereunto four pillars [of] shittim [wood], and overlaid them with gold: their hooks [were of] gold; and he cast for them four sockets of silver.
kjv.36:37: And he made an hanging for the tabernacle door [of] blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, of needlework;
kjv.36:38: And the five pillars of it with their hooks: and he overlaid their chapiters and their fillets with gold: but their five sockets [were of] brass.
kjv.37:1: And Bezaleel made the ark [of] shittim wood: two cubits and a half [was] the length of it, and a cubit and a half the breadth of it, and a cubit and a half the height of it:
kjv.37:2: And he overlaid it with pure gold within and without, and made a crown of gold to it round about.
kjv.37:3: And he cast for it four rings of gold, [to be set] by the four corners of it; even two rings upon the one side of it, and two rings upon the other side of it.
kjv.37:4: And he made staves [of] shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold.
kjv.37:5: And he put the staves into the rings by the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
kjv.37:6: And he made the mercy seat [of] pure gold: two cubits and a half [was] the length thereof, and one cubit and a half the breadth thereof.
kjv.37:7: And he made two cherubims [of] gold, beaten out of one piece made he them, on the two ends of the mercy seat;
kjv.37:8: One cherub on the end on this side, and another cherub on the [other] end on that side: out of the mercy seat made he the cherubims on the two ends thereof.
kjv.37:9: And the cherubims spread out [their] wings on high, [and] covered with their wings over the mercy seat, with their faces one to another; [even] to the mercy seatward were the faces of the cherubims.
kjv.37:10: And he made the table [of] shittim wood: two cubits [was] the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof:
kjv.37:11: And he overlaid it with pure gold, and made thereunto a crown of gold round about.
kjv.37:12: Also he made thereunto a border of an handbreadth round about; and made a crown of gold for the border thereof round about.
kjv.37:13: And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings upon the four corners that [were] in the four feet thereof.
kjv.37:14: Over against the border were the rings, the places for the staves to bear the table.
kjv.37:15: And he made the staves [of] shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold, to bear the table.
kjv.37:16: And he made the vessels which [were] upon the table, his dishes, and his spoons, and his bowls, and his covers to cover withal, [of] pure gold.
kjv.37:17: And he made the candlestick [of] pure gold: [of] beaten work made he the candlestick; his shaft, and his branch, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, were of the same:
kjv.37:18: And six branches going out of the sides thereof; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side thereof, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side thereof:
kjv.37:19: Three bowls made after the fashion of almonds in one branch, a knop and a flower; and three bowls made like almonds in another branch, a knop and a flower: so throughout the six branches going out of the candlestick.
kjv.37:20: And in the candlestick [were] four bowls made like almonds, his knops, and his flowers:
kjv.37:21: And a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, according to the six branches going out of it.
kjv.37:22: Their knops and their branches were of the same: all of it [was] one beaten work [of] pure gold.
kjv.37:23: And he made his seven lamps, and his snuffers, and his snuffdishes, [of] pure gold.
kjv.37:24: [Of] a talent of pure gold made he it, and all the vessels thereof.
kjv.37:25: And he made the incense altar [of] shittim wood: the length of it [was] a cubit, and the breadth of it a cubit; [it was] foursquare; and two cubits [was] the height of it; the horns thereof were of the same.
kjv.37:26: And he overlaid it with pure gold, [both] the top of it, and the sides thereof round about, and the horns of it: also he made unto it a crown of gold round about.
kjv.37:27: And he made two rings of gold for it under the crown thereof, by the two corners of it, upon the two sides thereof, to be places for the staves to bear it withal.
kjv.37:28: And he made the staves [of] shittim wood, and overlaid them with gold.
kjv.37:29: And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the apothecary.
kjv.38:1: And he made the altar of burnt offering [of] shittim wood: five cubits [was] the length thereof, and five cubits the breadth thereof; [it was] foursquare; and three cubits the height thereof.
kjv.38:2: And he made the horns thereof on the four corners of it; the horns thereof were of the same: and he overlaid it with brass.
kjv.38:3: And he made all the vessels of the altar, the pots, and the shovels, and the basons, [and] the fleshhooks, and the firepans: all the vessels thereof made he [of] brass.
kjv.38:4: And he made for the altar a brasen grate of network under the compass thereof beneath unto the midst of it.
kjv.38:5: And he cast four rings for the four ends of the grate of brass, [to be] places for the staves.
kjv.38:6: And he made the staves [of] shittim wood, and overlaid them with brass.
kjv.38:7: And he put the staves into the rings on the sides of the altar, to bear it withal; he made the altar hollow with boards.
kjv.38:8: And he made the laver [of] brass, and the foot of it [of] brass, of the lookingglasses of [the women] assembling, which assembled [at] the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
kjv.38:9: And he made the court: on the south side southward the hangings of the court [were of] fine twined linen, an hundred cubits:
kjv.38:10: Their pillars [were] twenty, and their brasen sockets twenty; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets [were of] silver.
kjv.38:11: And for the north side [the hangings were] an hundred cubits, their pillars [were] twenty, and their sockets of brass twenty; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets [of] silver.
kjv.38:12: And for the west side [were] hangings of fifty cubits, their pillars ten, and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets [of] silver.
kjv.38:13: And for the east side eastward fifty cubits.
kjv.38:14: The hangings of the one side [of the gate were] fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
kjv.38:15: And for the other side of the court gate, on this hand and that hand, [were] hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
kjv.38:16: All the hangings of the court round about [were] of fine twined linen.
kjv.38:17: And the sockets for the pillars [were of] brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets [of] silver; and the overlaying of their chapiters [of] silver; and all the pillars of the court [were] filleted with silver.
kjv.38:18: And the hanging for the gate of the court [was] needlework, [of] blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen: and twenty cubits [was] the length, and the height in the breadth [was] five cubits, answerable to the hangings of the court.
kjv.38:19: And their pillars [were] four, and their sockets [of] brass four; their hooks [of] silver, and the overlaying of their chapiters and their fillets [of] silver.
kjv.38:20: And all the pins of the tabernacle, and of the court round about, [were of] brass.
kjv.38:21: This is the sum of the tabernacle, [even] of the tabernacle of testimony, as it was counted, according to the commandment of Moses, [for] the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, son to Aaron the priest.
kjv.38:22: And Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.38:23: And with him [was] Aholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, and a cunning workman, and an embroiderer in blue, and in purple, and in scarlet, and fine linen.
kjv.38:24: All the gold that was occupied for the work in all the work of the holy [place], even the gold of the offering, was twenty and nine talents, and seven hundred and thirty shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary.
kjv.38:25: And the silver of them that were numbered of the congregation [was] an hundred talents, and a thousand seven hundred and threescore and fifteen shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary:
kjv.38:26: A bekah for every man, [that is], half a shekel, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for every one that went to be numbered, from twenty years old and upward, for six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty [men].
kjv.38:27: And of the hundred talents of silver were cast the sockets of the sanctuary, and the sockets of the vail; an hundred sockets of the hundred talents, a talent for a socket.
kjv.38:28: And of the thousand seven hundred seventy and five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, and overlaid their chapiters, and filleted them.
kjv.38:29: And the brass of the offering [was] seventy talents, and two thousand and four hundred shekels.
kjv.38:30: And therewith he made the sockets to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and the brasen altar, and the brasen grate for it, and all the vessels of the altar,
kjv.38:31: And the sockets of the court round about, and the sockets of the court gate, and all the pins of the tabernacle, and all the pins of the court round about.
kjv.39:1: And of the blue, and purple, and scarlet, they made cloths of service, to do service in the holy [place], and made the holy garments for Aaron; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.39:2: And he made the ephod [of] gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.
kjv.39:3: And they did beat the gold into thin plates, and cut [it into] wires, to work [it] in the blue, and in the purple, and in the scarlet, and in the fine linen, [with] cunning work.
kjv.39:4: They made shoulderpieces for it, to couple [it] together: by the two edges was it coupled together.
kjv.39:5: And the curious girdle of his ephod, that [was] upon it, [was] of the same, according to the work thereof; [of] gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.39:6: And they wrought onyx stones inclosed in ouches of gold, graven, as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel.
kjv.39:7: And he put them on the shoulders of the ephod, [that they should be] stones for a memorial to the children of Israel; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.39:8: And he made the breastplate [of] cunning work, like the work of the ephod; [of] gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.
kjv.39:9: It was foursquare; they made the breastplate double: a span [was] the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof, [being] doubled.
kjv.39:10: And they set in it four rows of stones: [the first] row [was] a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this [was] the first row.
kjv.39:11: And the second row, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.
kjv.39:12: And the third row, a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.
kjv.39:13: And the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper: [they were] inclosed in ouches of gold in their inclosings.
kjv.39:14: And the stones [were] according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, [like] the engravings of a signet, every one with his name, according to the twelve tribes.
kjv.39:15: And they made upon the breastplate chains at the ends, [of] wreathen work [of] pure gold.
kjv.39:16: And they made two ouches [of] gold, and two gold rings; and put the two rings in the two ends of the breastplate.
kjv.39:17: And they put the two wreathen chains of gold in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate.
kjv.39:18: And the two ends of the two wreathen chains they fastened in the two ouches, and put them on the shoulderpieces of the ephod, before it.
kjv.39:19: And they made two rings of gold, and put [them] on the two ends of the breastplate, upon the border of it, which [was] on the side of the ephod inward.
kjv.39:20: And they made two [other] golden rings, and put them on the two sides of the ephod underneath, toward the forepart of it, over against the [other] coupling thereof, above the curious girdle of the ephod.
kjv.39:21: And they did bind the breastplate by his rings unto the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it might be above the curious girdle of the ephod, and that the breastplate might not be loosed from the ephod; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.39:22: And he made the robe of the ephod [of] woven work, all [of] blue.
kjv.39:23: And [there was] an hole in the midst of the robe, as the hole of an habergeon, [with] a band round about the hole, that it should not rend.
kjv.39:24: And they made upon the hems of the robe pomegranates [of] blue, and purple, and scarlet, [and] twined [linen].
kjv.39:25: And they made bells [of] pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates upon the hem of the robe, round about between the pomegranates;
kjv.39:26: A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, round about the hem of the robe to minister [in]; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.39:27: And they made coats [of] fine linen [of] woven work for Aaron, and for his sons,
kjv.39:28: And a mitre [of] fine linen, and goodly bonnets [of] fine linen, and linen breeches [of] fine twined linen,
kjv.39:29: And a girdle [of] fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, [of] needlework; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.39:30: And they made the plate of the holy crown [of] pure gold, and wrote upon it a writing, [like to] the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
kjv.39:31: And they tied unto it a lace of blue, to fasten [it] on high upon the mitre; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.39:32: Thus was all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation finished: and the children of Israel did according to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so did they.
kjv.39:33: And they brought the tabernacle unto Moses, the tent, and all his furniture, his taches, his boards, his bars, and his pillars, and his sockets,
kjv.39:34: And the covering of rams' skins dyed red, and the covering of badgers' skins, and the vail of the covering,
kjv.39:35: The ark of the testimony, and the staves thereof, and the mercy seat,
kjv.39:36: The table, [and] all the vessels thereof, and the shewbread,
kjv.39:37: The pure candlestick, [with] the lamps thereof, [even with] the lamps to be set in order, and all the vessels thereof, and the oil for light,
kjv.39:38: And the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the sweet incense, and the hanging for the tabernacle door,
kjv.39:39: The brasen altar, and his grate of brass, his staves, and all his vessels, the laver and his foot,
kjv.39:40: The hangings of the court, his pillars, and his sockets, and the hanging for the court gate, his cords, and his pins, and all the vessels of the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of the congregation,
kjv.39:41: The cloths of service to do service in the holy [place], and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons' garments, to minister in the priest's office.
kjv.39:42: According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work.
kjv.39:43: And Moses did look upon all the work, and, behold, they had done it as the LORD had commanded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them.
kjv.40:1: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
kjv.40:2: On the first day of the first month shalt thou set up the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation.
kjv.40:3: And thou shalt put therein the ark of the testimony, and cover the ark with the vail.
kjv.40:4: And thou shalt bring in the table, and set in order the things that are to be set in order upon it; and thou shalt bring in the candlestick, and light the lamps thereof.
kjv.40:5: And thou shalt set the altar of gold for the incense before the ark of the testimony, and put the hanging of the door to the tabernacle.
kjv.40:6: And thou shalt set the altar of the burnt offering before the door of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation.
kjv.40:7: And thou shalt set the laver between the tent of the congregation and the altar, and shalt put water therein.
kjv.40:8: And thou shalt set up the court round about, and hang up the hanging at the court gate.
kjv.40:9: And thou shalt take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle, and all that [is] therein, and shalt hallow it, and all the vessels thereof: and it shall be holy.
kjv.40:10: And thou shalt anoint the altar of the burnt offering, and all his vessels, and sanctify the altar: and it shall be an altar most holy.
kjv.40:11: And thou shalt anoint the laver and his foot, and sanctify it.
kjv.40:12: And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and wash them with water.
kjv.40:13: And thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments, and anoint him, and sanctify him; that he may minister unto me in the priest's office.
kjv.40:14: And thou shalt bring his sons, and clothe them with coats:
kjv.40:15: And thou shalt anoint them, as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister unto me in the priest's office: for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.
kjv.40:16: Thus did Moses: according to all that the LORD commanded him, so did he.
kjv.40:17: And it came to pass in the first month in the second year, on the first [day] of the month, [that] the tabernacle was reared up.
kjv.40:18: And Moses reared up the tabernacle, and fastened his sockets, and set up the boards thereof, and put in the bars thereof, and reared up his pillars.
kjv.40:19: And he spread abroad the tent over the tabernacle, and put the covering of the tent above upon it; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.40:20: And he took and put the testimony into the ark, and set the staves on the ark, and put the mercy seat above upon the ark:
kjv.40:21: And he brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the vail of the covering, and covered the ark of the testimony; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.40:22: And he put the table in the tent of the congregation, upon the side of the tabernacle northward, without the vail.
kjv.40:23: And he set the bread in order upon it before the LORD; as the LORD had commanded Moses.
kjv.40:24: And he put the candlestick in the tent of the congregation, over against the table, on the side of the tabernacle southward.
kjv.40:25: And he lighted the lamps before the LORD; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.40:26: And he put the golden altar in the tent of the congregation before the vail:
kjv.40:27: And he burnt sweet incense thereon; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.40:28: And he set up the hanging [at] the door of the tabernacle.
kjv.40:29: And he put the altar of burnt offering [by] the door of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation, and offered upon it the burnt offering and the meat offering; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.40:30: And he set the laver between the tent of the congregation and the altar, and put water there, to wash [withal].
kjv.40:31: And Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet thereat:
kjv.40:32: When they went into the tent of the congregation, and when they came near unto the altar, they washed; as the LORD commanded Moses.
kjv.40:33: And he reared up the court round about the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the hanging of the court gate. So Moses finished the work.
kjv.40:34: Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
kjv.40:35: And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of the congregation, because the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
kjv.40:36: And when the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys:
kjv.40:37: But if the cloud were not taken up, then they journeyed not till the day that it was taken up.
kjv.40:38: For the cloud of the LORD [was] upon the tabernacle by day, and fire was on it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.

bsb.1:1: These are the names of the sons of Israel who went to Egypt with Jacob, each with his family:
bsb.1:4: Dan and Naphtali; Gad and Asher.
bsb.1:5: The descendants of Jacob numbered seventy in all, including Joseph, who was already in Egypt.
bsb.1:6: Now Joseph and all his brothers and all that generation died,
bsb.1:7: but the Israelites were fruitful and increased rapidly; they multiplied and became exceedingly numerous, so that the land was filled with them.
bsb.1:8: Then a new king, who did not know Joseph, came to power in Egypt.
bsb.1:9: “Look,” he said to his people, “the Israelites have become too numerous and too powerful for us.
bsb.1:10: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, or they will increase even more; and if a war breaks out, they may join our enemies, fight against us, and leave the country.”
bsb.1:11: So the Egyptians appointed taskmasters over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor. As a result, they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.
bsb.1:12: But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and flourished; so the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites.
bsb.1:14: and made their lives bitter with hard labor in brick and mortar, and with all kinds of work in the fields. Every service they imposed was harsh.
bsb.1:15: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, whose names were Shiphrah and Puah,
bsb.1:16: “When you help the Hebrew women give birth, observe them on the birthstools. If the child is a son, kill him; but if it is a daughter, let her live.”
bsb.1:17: The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.
bsb.1:18: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, “Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?”
bsb.1:19: The midwives answered Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they are vigorous and give birth before a midwife arrives.”
bsb.1:20: So God was good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and became even more numerous.
bsb.1:21: And because the midwives feared God, He gave them families of their own.
bsb.1:22: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people: “Every son born to the Hebrews you must throw into the Nile, but every daughter you may allow to live.”
bsb.2:1: Now a man of the house of Levi married a daughter of Levi,
bsb.2:2: and she conceived and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a beautiful child, she hid him for three months.
bsb.2:3: But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in the basket and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.
bsb.2:4: And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.
bsb.2:5: Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile, and her attendants were walking along the riverbank. And when she saw the basket among the reeds, she sent her maidservant to retrieve it.
bsb.2:6: When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”
bsb.2:7: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?”
bsb.2:8: “Go ahead,” Pharaoh’s daughter told her. And the girl went and called the boy’s mother.
bsb.2:9: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.” So the woman took the boy and nursed him.
bsb.2:10: When the child had grown older, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.”
bsb.2:11: One day, after Moses had grown up, he went out to his own people and observed their hard labor. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.
bsb.2:12: After looking this way and that and seeing no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
bsb.2:13: The next day Moses went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, “Why are you attacking your companion?”
bsb.2:14: But the man replied, “Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you planning to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?” Then Moses was afraid and thought, “This thing I have done has surely become known.”
bsb.2:15: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, where he sat down beside a well.
bsb.2:16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father’s flock.
bsb.2:17: And when some shepherds came along and drove them away, Moses rose up to help them and watered their flock.
bsb.2:18: When the daughters returned to their father Reuel, he asked them, “Why have you returned so early today?”
bsb.2:19: “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds,” they replied. “He even drew water for us and watered the flock.”
bsb.2:20: “So where is he?” their father asked. “Why did you leave the man behind? Invite him to have something to eat.”
bsb.2:21: Moses agreed to stay with the man, and he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage.
bsb.2:22: And she gave birth to a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, “I have become a foreigner in a foreign land.”
bsb.2:23: After a long time, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned and cried out under their burden of slavery, and their cry for deliverance from bondage ascended to God.
bsb.2:24: So God heard their groaning, and He remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
bsb.2:25: God saw the Israelites and took notice.
bsb.3:1: Meanwhile, Moses was shepherding the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
bsb.3:2: There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a blazing fire from within a bush. Moses saw the bush ablaze with fire, but it was not consumed.
bsb.3:3: So Moses thought, “I must go over and see this marvelous sight. Why is the bush not burning up?”
bsb.3:4: When the LORD saw that he had gone over to look, God called out to him from within the bush, “Moses, Moses!” “Here I am,” he answered.
bsb.3:5: “Do not come any closer,” God said. “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.”
bsb.3:6: Then He said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” At this, Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.
bsb.3:7: The LORD said, “I have indeed seen the affliction of My people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their oppressors, and I am aware of their sufferings.
bsb.3:8: I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey—the home of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
bsb.3:9: And now the cry of the Israelites has reached Me, and I have seen how severely the Egyptians are oppressing them.
bsb.3:10: Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.”
bsb.3:11: But Moses asked God, “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?”
bsb.3:12: “I will surely be with you,” God said, “and this will be the sign to you that I have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Egypt, all of you will worship God on this mountain.”
bsb.3:13: Then Moses asked God, “Suppose I go to the Israelites and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they ask me, ‘What is His name?’ What should I tell them?”
bsb.3:14: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM. This is what you are to say to the Israelites: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
bsb.3:15: God also told Moses, “Say to the Israelites, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.
bsb.3:16: Go, assemble the elders of Israel and say to them, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—has appeared to me and said: I have surely attended to you and have seen what has been done to you in Egypt.
bsb.3:17: And I have promised to bring you up out of your affliction in Egypt, into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—a land flowing with milk and honey.’
bsb.3:18: The elders of Israel will listen to what you say, and you must go with them to the king of Egypt and tell him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Now please let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.’
bsb.3:19: But I know that the king of Egypt will not allow you to go unless a mighty hand compels him.
bsb.3:20: So I will stretch out My hand and strike the Egyptians with all the wonders I will perform among them. And after that, he will release you.
bsb.3:21: And I will grant this people such favor in the sight of the Egyptians that when you leave, you will not go away empty-handed.
bsb.3:22: Every woman shall ask her neighbor and any woman staying in her house for silver and gold jewelry and clothing, and you will put them on your sons and daughters. So you will plunder the Egyptians.”
bsb.4:1: Then Moses answered, “What if they do not believe me or listen to my voice? For they may say, ‘The LORD has not appeared to you.’”
bsb.4:2: And the LORD asked him, “What is that in your hand?” “A staff,” he replied.
bsb.4:3: “Throw it on the ground,” said the LORD. So Moses threw it on the ground, and it became a snake, and he ran from it.
bsb.4:4: “Stretch out your hand and grab it by the tail,” the LORD said to Moses, who reached out his hand and caught the snake, and it turned back into a staff in his hand.
bsb.4:5: “This is so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has appeared to you.”
bsb.4:6: Furthermore, the LORD said to Moses, “Put your hand inside your cloak.” So he put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out, his hand was leprous, white as snow.
bsb.4:7: “Put your hand back inside your cloak,” said the LORD. So Moses put his hand back inside his cloak, and when he took it out, it was restored, like the rest of his skin.
bsb.4:8: And the LORD said, “If they refuse to believe you or heed the witness of the first sign, they may believe that of the second.
bsb.4:9: But if they do not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. Then the water you take from the Nile will become blood on the ground.”
bsb.4:10: “Please, Lord,” Moses replied, “I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since You have spoken to Your servant, for I am slow of speech and tongue.”
bsb.4:11: And the LORD said to him, “Who gave man his mouth? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the sighted or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
bsb.4:12: Now go! I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.”
bsb.4:13: But Moses replied, “Please, Lord, send someone else.”
bsb.4:14: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Moses, and He said, “Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well, and he is now on his way to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.
bsb.4:15: You are to speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I will help both of you to speak, and I will teach you what to do.
bsb.4:16: He will speak to the people for you. He will be your spokesman, and it will be as if you were God to him.
bsb.4:17: But take this staff in your hand so you can perform signs with it.”
bsb.4:18: Then Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said to him, “Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt to see if they are still alive.” “Go in peace,” Jethro replied.
bsb.4:19: Now the LORD had said to Moses in Midian, “Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.”
bsb.4:20: So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey, and headed back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.
bsb.4:21: The LORD instructed Moses, “When you go back to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders that I have put within your power. But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.
bsb.4:22: Then tell Pharaoh that this is what the LORD says: ‘Israel is My firstborn son,
bsb.4:23: and I told you to let My son go so that he may worship Me. But since you have refused to let him go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son!’”
bsb.4:24: Now at a lodging place along the way, the LORD met Moses and was about to kill him.
bsb.4:25: But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son’s foreskin, and touched it to Moses’ feet. “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me,” she said.
bsb.4:26: So the LORD let him alone. (When she said, “bridegroom of blood,” she was referring to the circumcision.)
bsb.4:27: Meanwhile, the LORD had said to Aaron, “Go and meet Moses in the wilderness.” So he went and met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.
bsb.4:28: And Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and all the signs He had commanded him to perform.
bsb.4:29: Then Moses and Aaron went and assembled all the elders of the Israelites,
bsb.4:30: and Aaron relayed everything the LORD had said to Moses. And Moses performed the signs before the people,
bsb.4:31: and they believed. And when they heard that the LORD had attended to the Israelites and had seen their affliction, they bowed down and worshiped.
bsb.5:1: After that, Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.’”
bsb.5:2: But Pharaoh replied, “Who is the LORD that I should obey His voice and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and I will not let Israel go.”
bsb.5:3: “The God of the Hebrews has met with us,” they answered. “Please let us go on a three-day journey into the wilderness to sacrifice to the LORD our God, or He may strike us with plagues or with the sword.”
bsb.5:4: But the king of Egypt said to them, “Moses and Aaron, why do you draw the people away from their work? Get back to your labor!”
bsb.5:5: Pharaoh also said, “Look, the people of the land are now numerous, and you would be stopping them from their labor.”
bsb.5:6: That same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people and their foremen:
bsb.5:7: “You shall no longer supply the people with straw for making bricks. They must go and gather their own straw.
bsb.5:8: But require of them the same quota of bricks as before; do not reduce it. For they are lazy; that is why they are crying out, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to our God.’
bsb.5:9: Make the work harder on the men so they will be occupied and pay no attention to these lies.”
bsb.5:10: So the taskmasters and foremen of the people went out and said to them, “This is what Pharaoh says: ‘I am no longer giving you straw.
bsb.5:11: Go and get your own straw wherever you can find it; but your workload will in no way be reduced.’”
bsb.5:12: So the people scattered all over the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
bsb.5:13: The taskmasters kept pressing them, saying, “Fulfill your quota each day, just as you did when straw was provided.”
bsb.5:14: Then the Israelite foremen, whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over the people, were beaten and asked, “Why have you not fulfilled your quota of bricks yesterday or today, as you did before?”
bsb.5:15: So the Israelite foremen went and appealed to Pharaoh: “Why are you treating your servants this way?
bsb.5:16: No straw has been given to your servants, yet we are told, ‘Make bricks!’ Look, your servants are being beaten, but the fault is with your own people.”
bsb.5:17: “You are slackers!” Pharaoh replied. “Slackers! That is why you keep saying, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.’
bsb.5:18: Now get to work. You will be given no straw, yet you must deliver the full quota of bricks.”
bsb.5:19: The Israelite foremen realized they were in trouble when they were told, “You must not reduce your daily quota of bricks.”
bsb.5:20: When they left Pharaoh, they confronted Moses and Aaron, who stood waiting to meet them.
bsb.5:21: “May the LORD look upon you and judge you,” the foremen said, “for you have made us a stench before Pharaoh and his officials; you have placed in their hand a sword to kill us!”
bsb.5:22: So Moses returned to the LORD and asked, “Lord, why have You brought trouble upon this people? Is this why You sent me?
bsb.5:23: Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has brought trouble on this people, and You have not delivered Your people in any way.”
bsb.6:1: But the LORD said to Moses, “Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh, for because of My mighty hand he will let the people go; because of My strong hand he will drive them out of his land.”
bsb.6:2: God also told Moses, “I am the LORD.
bsb.6:3: I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty, but by My name the LORD I did not make Myself known to them.
bsb.6:4: I also established My covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan, the land where they lived as foreigners.
bsb.6:5: Furthermore, I have heard the groaning of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians are enslaving, and I have remembered My covenant.
bsb.6:6: Therefore tell the Israelites: ‘I am the LORD, and I will bring you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians and deliver you from their bondage. I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with mighty acts of judgment.
bsb.6:7: I will take you as My own people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians.
bsb.6:8: And I will bring you into the land that I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to you as a possession. I am the LORD!’”
bsb.6:9: Moses relayed this message to the Israelites, but on account of their broken spirit and cruel bondage, they did not listen to him.
bsb.6:10: So the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.6:11: “Go and tell Pharaoh king of Egypt to let the Israelites go out of his land.”
bsb.6:12: But in the LORD’s presence Moses replied, “If the Israelites will not listen to me, then why would Pharaoh listen to me, since I am unskilled in speech?”
bsb.6:13: Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron and gave them a charge concerning both the Israelites and Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the Israelites out of the land of Egypt.
bsb.6:14: These were the heads of their fathers’ houses: The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, were Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi. These were the clans of Reuben.
bsb.6:15: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman. These were the clans of Simeon.
bsb.6:16: These were the names of the sons of Levi according to their records: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.
bsb.6:17: The sons of Gershon were Libni and Shimei, by their clans.
bsb.6:18: The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.
bsb.6:19: The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of the Levites according to their records.
bsb.6:20: And Amram married his father’s sister Jochebed, and she bore him Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years.
bsb.6:21: The sons of Izhar were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
bsb.6:22: The sons of Uzziel were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
bsb.6:23: And Aaron married Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon, and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
bsb.6:24: The sons of Korah were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. These were the clans of the Korahites.
bsb.6:25: Aaron’s son Eleazar married one of the daughters of Putiel, and she bore him Phinehas. These were the heads of the Levite families by their clans.
bsb.6:26: It was this Aaron and Moses to whom the LORD said, “Bring the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions.”
bsb.6:27: Moses and Aaron were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt in order to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
bsb.6:28: Now on the day that the LORD spoke to Moses in Egypt,
bsb.6:29: He said to him, “I am the LORD; tell Pharaoh king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
bsb.6:30: But in the LORD’s presence Moses replied, “Since I am unskilled in speech, why would Pharaoh listen to me?”
bsb.7:1: The LORD answered Moses, “See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.
bsb.7:2: You are to speak all that I command you, and your brother Aaron is to tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his land.
bsb.7:3: But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and though I will multiply My signs and wonders in the land of Egypt,
bsb.7:4: Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay My hand on Egypt, and by mighty acts of judgment I will bring the divisions of My people the Israelites out of the land of Egypt.
bsb.7:5: And the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD, when I stretch out My hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them.”
bsb.7:6: So Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded them.
bsb.7:7: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.
bsb.7:8: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
bsb.7:9: “When Pharaoh tells you, ‘Perform a miracle,’ you are to say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh,’ and it will become a serpent.”
bsb.7:10: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the LORD had commanded. Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a serpent.
bsb.7:11: But Pharaoh called the wise men and sorcerers and magicians of Egypt, and they also did the same things by their magic arts.
bsb.7:12: Each one threw down his staff, and it became a serpent. But Aaron’s staff swallowed up the other staffs.
bsb.7:13: Still, Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
bsb.7:14: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh’s heart is unyielding; he refuses to let the people go.
bsb.7:15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning as you see him walking out to the water. Wait on the bank of the Nile to meet him, and take in your hand the staff that was changed into a snake.
bsb.7:16: Then say to him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to tell you: Let My people go, so that they may worship Me in the wilderness. But you have not listened until now.
bsb.7:17: This is what the LORD says: By this you will know that I am the LORD. Behold, with the staff in my hand I will strike the water of the Nile, and it will turn to blood.
bsb.7:18: The fish in the Nile will die, the river will stink, and the Egyptians will be unable to drink its water.’”
bsb.7:19: And the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt—over their rivers and canals and ponds and reservoirs—that they may become blood.’ There will be blood throughout the land of Egypt, even in the vessels of wood and stone.”
bsb.7:20: Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded; in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials, Aaron raised the staff and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water was turned to blood.
bsb.7:21: The fish in the Nile died, and the river smelled so bad that the Egyptians could not drink its water. And there was blood throughout the land of Egypt.
bsb.7:22: But the magicians of Egypt did the same things by their magic arts. So Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
bsb.7:23: Instead, Pharaoh turned around, went into his palace, and did not take any of this to heart.
bsb.7:24: So all the Egyptians dug around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink the water from the river.
bsb.7:25: And seven full days passed after the LORD had struck the Nile.
bsb.8:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him that this is what the LORD says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
bsb.8:2: But if you refuse to let them go, I will plague your whole country with frogs.
bsb.8:3: The Nile will teem with frogs, and they will come into your palace and up to your bedroom and onto your bed, into the houses of your officials and your people, and into your ovens and kneading bowls.
bsb.8:4: The frogs will come up on you and your people and all your officials.’”
bsb.8:5: And the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers and canals and ponds, and cause the frogs to come up onto the land of Egypt.’”
bsb.8:6: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
bsb.8:7: But the magicians did the same thing by their magic arts, and they also brought frogs up onto the land of Egypt.
bsb.8:8: Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Pray to the LORD to take the frogs away from me and my people. Then I will let your people go, that they may sacrifice to the LORD.”
bsb.8:9: Moses said to Pharaoh, “You may have the honor over me. When shall I pray for you and your officials and your people that the frogs (except for those in the Nile) may be taken away from you and your houses?”
bsb.8:10: “Tomorrow,” Pharaoh answered. “May it be as you say,” Moses replied, “so that you may know that there is no one like the LORD our God.
bsb.8:11: The frogs will depart from you and your houses and your officials and your people; they will remain only in the Nile.”
bsb.8:12: After Moses and Aaron had left Pharaoh, Moses cried out to the LORD for help with the frogs that He had brought against Pharaoh.
bsb.8:13: And the LORD did as Moses requested, and the frogs in the houses, the courtyards, and the fields died.
bsb.8:14: They were piled into countless heaps, and there was a terrible stench in the land.
bsb.8:15: When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, however, he hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
bsb.8:16: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth, that it may turn into swarms of gnats throughout the land of Egypt.’”
bsb.8:17: This they did, and when Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the earth, gnats came upon man and beast. All the dust of the earth turned into gnats throughout the land of Egypt.
bsb.8:18: The magicians tried to produce gnats using their magic arts, but they could not. And the gnats remained on man and beast.
bsb.8:19: “This is the finger of God,” the magicians said to Pharaoh. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
bsb.8:20: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning, and when Pharaoh goes out to the water, stand before him and tell him that this is what the LORD says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
bsb.8:21: But if you will not let My people go, I will send swarms of flies upon you and your officials and your people and your houses. The houses of the Egyptians and even the ground where they stand will be full of flies.
bsb.8:22: But on that day I will give special treatment to the land of Goshen, where My people live; no swarms of flies will be found there. In this way you will know that I, the LORD, am in the land.
bsb.8:23: I will make a distinction between My people and your people. This sign will take place tomorrow.’”
bsb.8:24: And the LORD did so. Thick swarms of flies poured into Pharaoh’s palace and into the houses of his officials. Throughout Egypt the land was ruined by swarms of flies.
bsb.8:25: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Go, sacrifice to your God within this land.”
bsb.8:26: But Moses replied, “It would not be right to do that, because the sacrifices we offer to the LORD our God would be detestable to the Egyptians. If we offer sacrifices that are detestable before the Egyptians, will they not stone us?
bsb.8:27: We must make a three-day journey into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God as He commands us.”
bsb.8:28: Pharaoh answered, “I will let you go and sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness, but you must not go very far. Now pray for me.”
bsb.8:29: “As soon as I leave you,” Moses said, “I will pray to the LORD, so that tomorrow the swarms of flies will depart from Pharaoh and his officials and his people. But Pharaoh must not act deceitfully again by refusing to let the people go and sacrifice to the LORD.”
bsb.8:30: Then Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD,
bsb.8:31: and the LORD did as Moses requested. He removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh and his officials and his people; not one fly remained.
bsb.8:32: But Pharaoh hardened his heart this time as well, and he would not let the people go.
bsb.9:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him that this is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
bsb.9:2: But if you continue to restrain them and refuse to let them go,
bsb.9:3: then the hand of the LORD will bring a severe plague on your livestock in the field—on your horses, donkeys, camels, herds, and flocks.
bsb.9:4: But the LORD will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that no animal belonging to the Israelites will die.’”
bsb.9:5: The LORD set a time, saying, “Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land.”
bsb.9:6: And the next day the LORD did just that. All the livestock of the Egyptians died, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites died.
bsb.9:7: Pharaoh sent officials and found that none of the livestock of the Israelites had died. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the people go.
bsb.9:8: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Take handfuls of soot from the furnace; in the sight of Pharaoh, Moses is to toss it into the air.
bsb.9:9: It will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and festering boils will break out on man and beast throughout the land.”
bsb.9:10: So they took soot from the furnace and stood before Pharaoh. Moses tossed it into the air, and festering boils broke out on man and beast.
bsb.9:11: The magicians could not stand before Moses, because the boils had broken out on them and on all the Egyptians.
bsb.9:12: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said to Moses.
bsb.9:13: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning, stand before Pharaoh, and tell him that this is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
bsb.9:14: Otherwise, I will send all My plagues against you and your officials and your people, so you may know that there is no one like Me in all the earth.
bsb.9:15: For by this time I could have stretched out My hand and struck you and your people with a plague to wipe you off the earth.
bsb.9:16: But I have raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power to you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.
bsb.9:17: Still, you lord it over My people and do not allow them to go.
bsb.9:18: Behold, at this time tomorrow I will rain down the worst hail that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded until now.
bsb.9:19: So give orders now to shelter your livestock and everything you have in the field. Every man or beast that remains in the field and is not brought inside will die when the hail comes down upon them.’”
bsb.9:20: Those among Pharaoh’s officials who feared the word of the LORD hurried to bring their servants and livestock to shelter,
bsb.9:21: but those who disregarded the word of the LORD left their servants and livestock in the field.
bsb.9:22: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that hail may fall on all the land of Egypt—on man and beast and every plant of the field throughout the land of Egypt.”
bsb.9:23: So Moses stretched out his staff toward heaven, and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and lightning struck the earth. So the LORD rained down hail upon the land of Egypt.
bsb.9:24: The hail fell and the lightning continued flashing through it. The hail was so severe that nothing like it had ever been seen in all the land of Egypt from the time it became a nation.
bsb.9:25: Throughout the land of Egypt, the hail struck down everything in the field, both man and beast; it beat down every plant of the field and stripped every tree.
bsb.9:26: The only place where it did not hail was in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived.
bsb.9:27: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron. “This time I have sinned,” he said. “The LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
bsb.9:28: Pray to the LORD, for there has been enough of God’s thunder and hail. I will let you go; you do not need to stay any longer.”
bsb.9:29: Moses said to him, “When I have left the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD. The thunder will cease, and there will be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth is the LORD’s.
bsb.9:30: But as for you and your officials, I know that you still do not fear the LORD our God.”
bsb.9:31: (Now the flax and barley were destroyed, since the barley was ripe and the flax was in bloom;
bsb.9:32: but the wheat and spelt were not destroyed, because they are late crops.)
bsb.9:33: Then Moses departed from Pharaoh, went out of the city, and spread out his hands to the LORD. The thunder and hail ceased, and the rain no longer poured down on the land.
bsb.9:34: When Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had ceased, he sinned again and hardened his heart—he and his officials.
bsb.9:35: So Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had said through Moses.
bsb.10:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, that I may perform these miraculous signs of Mine among them,
bsb.10:2: and that you may tell your children and grandchildren how severely I dealt with the Egyptians when I performed miraculous signs among them, so that all of you may know that I am the LORD.”
bsb.10:3: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and told him, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
bsb.10:4: But if you refuse to let My people go, I will bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.
bsb.10:5: They will cover the face of the land so that no one can see it. They will devour whatever is left after the hail and eat every tree that grows in your fields.
bsb.10:6: They will fill your houses and the houses of all your officials and every Egyptian—something neither your fathers nor your grandfathers have seen since the day they came into this land.’” Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh’s presence.
bsb.10:7: Pharaoh’s officials asked him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the LORD their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt is in ruins?”
bsb.10:8: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. “Go, worship the LORD your God,” he said. “But who exactly will be going?”
bsb.10:9: “We will go with our young and old,” Moses replied. “We will go with our sons and daughters, and with our flocks and herds, for we must hold a feast to the LORD.”
bsb.10:10: Then Pharaoh told them, “May the LORD be with you if I ever let you go with your little ones. Clearly you are bent on evil.
bsb.10:11: No, only the men may go and worship the LORD, since that is what you have been requesting.” And Moses and Aaron were driven from Pharaoh’s presence.
bsb.10:12: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, so that the locusts may swarm over it and devour every plant in the land—everything that the hail has left behind.”
bsb.10:13: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and throughout that day and night the LORD sent an east wind across the land. By morning the east wind had brought the locusts.
bsb.10:14: The locusts swarmed across the land and settled over the entire territory of Egypt. Never before had there been so many locusts, and never again will there be.
bsb.10:15: They covered the face of all the land until it was black, and they consumed all the plants on the ground and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had left behind. Nothing green was left on any tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.
bsb.10:16: Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
bsb.10:17: Now please forgive my sin once more and appeal to the LORD your God, that He may remove this death from me.”
bsb.10:18: So Moses left Pharaoh’s presence and appealed to the LORD.
bsb.10:19: And the LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind that carried off the locusts and blew them into the Red Sea. Not a single locust remained anywhere in Egypt.
bsb.10:20: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.
bsb.10:21: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that darkness may spread over the land of Egypt—a palpable darkness.”
bsb.10:22: So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and total darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.
bsb.10:23: No one could see anyone else, and for three days no one left his place. Yet all the Israelites had light in their dwellings.
bsb.10:24: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, “Go, worship the LORD. Even your little ones may go with you; only your flocks and herds must stay behind.”
bsb.10:25: But Moses replied, “You must also provide us with sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the LORD our God.
bsb.10:26: Even our livestock must go with us; not a hoof will be left behind, for we will need some of them to worship the LORD our God, and we will not know how we are to worship the LORD until we arrive.”
bsb.10:27: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
bsb.10:28: “Depart from me!” Pharaoh said to Moses. “Make sure you never see my face again, for on the day you see my face, you will die.”
bsb.10:29: “As you say,” Moses replied, “I will never see your face again.”
bsb.11:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, “I will bring upon Pharaoh and Egypt one more plague. After that, he will allow you to leave this place. And when he lets you go, he will drive you out completely.
bsb.11:2: Now announce to the people that men and women alike should ask their neighbors for articles of silver and gold.”
bsb.11:3: And the LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover, Moses himself was highly regarded in Egypt by Pharaoh’s officials and by the people.
bsb.11:4: So Moses declared, “This is what the LORD says: ‘About midnight I will go throughout Egypt,
bsb.11:5: and every firstborn son in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the servant girl behind the hand mill, as well as the firstborn of all the cattle.
bsb.11:6: Then a great cry will go out over all the land of Egypt. Such an outcry has never been heard before and will never be heard again.
bsb.11:7: But among all the Israelites, not even a dog will snarl at man or beast.’ Then you will know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.
bsb.11:8: And all these officials of yours will come and bow before me, saying, ‘Go, you and all the people who follow you!’ After that, I will depart.” And hot with anger, Moses left Pharaoh’s presence.
bsb.11:9: The LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that My wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.”
bsb.11:10: Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh, but the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart so that he would not let the Israelites go out of his land.
bsb.12:1: Now the LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt,
bsb.12:2: “This month is the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of your year.
bsb.12:3: Tell the whole congregation of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each man must select a lamb for his family, one per household.
bsb.12:4: If the household is too small for a whole lamb, they are to share with the nearest neighbor based on the number of people, and apportion the lamb accordingly.
bsb.12:5: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male, and you may take it from the sheep or the goats.
bsb.12:6: You must keep it until the fourteenth day of the month, when the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel will slaughter the animals at twilight.
bsb.12:7: They are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs.
bsb.12:8: They are to eat the meat that night, roasted over the fire, along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
bsb.12:9: Do not eat any of the meat raw or cooked in boiling water, but only roasted over the fire—its head and legs and inner parts.
bsb.12:10: Do not leave any of it until morning; before the morning you must burn up any part that is left over.
bsb.12:11: This is how you are to eat it: You must be fully dressed for travel, with your sandals on your feet and your staff in your hand. You are to eat in haste; it is the LORD’s Passover.
bsb.12:12: On that night I will pass through the land of Egypt and strike down every firstborn male, both man and beast, and I will execute judgment against all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
bsb.12:13: The blood on the houses where you are staying will distinguish them; when I see the blood, I will pass over you. No plague will fall on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
bsb.12:14: And this day will be a memorial for you, and you are to celebrate it as a feast to the LORD, as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
bsb.12:15: For seven days you must eat unleavened bread. On the first day you are to remove the leaven from your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened from the first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel.
bsb.12:16: On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly, and another on the seventh day. You must not do any work on those days, except to prepare the meals—that is all you may do.
bsb.12:17: So you are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt. You must keep this day as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
bsb.12:18: In the first month you are to eat unleavened bread, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day.
bsb.12:19: For seven days there must be no leaven found in your houses. If anyone eats something leavened, that person, whether a foreigner or native of the land, must be cut off from the congregation of Israel.
bsb.12:20: You are not to eat anything leavened; eat unleavened bread in all your homes.”
bsb.12:21: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and told them, “Go at once and select for yourselves a lamb for each family, and slaughter the Passover lamb.
bsb.12:22: Take a cluster of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin, and brush the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe. None of you shall go out the door of his house until morning.
bsb.12:23: When the LORD passes through to strike down the Egyptians, He will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway; so He will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down.
bsb.12:24: And you are to keep this command as a permanent statute for you and your descendants.
bsb.12:25: When you enter the land that the LORD will give you as He promised, you are to keep this service.
bsb.12:26: When your children ask you, ‘What does this service mean to you?’
bsb.12:27: you are to reply, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt when He struck down the Egyptians and spared our homes.’” Then the people bowed down and worshiped.
bsb.12:28: And the Israelites went and did just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
bsb.12:29: Now at midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn male in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on his throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner in the dungeon, as well as all the firstborn among the livestock.
bsb.12:30: During the night Pharaoh got up—he and all his officials and all the Egyptians—and there was loud wailing in Egypt; for there was no house without someone dead.
bsb.12:31: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron by night and said, “Get up, leave my people, both you and the Israelites! Go, worship the LORD as you have requested.
bsb.12:32: Take your flocks and herds as well, just as you have said, and depart! And bless me also.”
bsb.12:33: And in order to send them out of the land quickly, the Egyptians urged the people on. “For otherwise,” they said, “we are all going to die!”
bsb.12:34: So the people took their dough before it was leavened, carrying it on their shoulders in kneading bowls wrapped in clothing.
bsb.12:35: Furthermore, the Israelites acted on Moses’ word and asked the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold, and for clothing.
bsb.12:36: And the LORD gave the people such favor in the sight of the Egyptians that they granted their request. In this way they plundered the Egyptians.
bsb.12:37: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children.
bsb.12:38: And a mixed multitude also went up with them, along with great droves of livestock, both flocks and herds.
bsb.12:39: Since their dough had no leaven, the people baked what they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened loaves. For when they had been driven out of Egypt, they could not delay and had not prepared any provisions for themselves.
bsb.12:40: Now the duration of the Israelites’ stay in Egypt was 430 years.
bsb.12:41: At the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the LORD’s divisions went out of the land of Egypt.
bsb.12:42: Because the LORD kept a vigil that night to bring them out of the land of Egypt, this same night is to be a vigil to the LORD, to be observed by all the Israelites for the generations to come.
bsb.12:43: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the statute of the Passover: No foreigner is to eat of it.
bsb.12:44: But any slave who has been purchased may eat of it, after you have circumcised him.
bsb.12:45: A temporary resident or hired hand shall not eat the Passover.
bsb.12:46: It must be eaten inside one house. You are not to take any of the meat outside the house, and you may not break any of the bones.
bsb.12:47: The whole congregation of Israel must celebrate it.
bsb.12:48: If a foreigner resides with you and wants to celebrate the LORD’s Passover, all the males in the household must be circumcised; then he may come near to celebrate it, and he shall be like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised man may eat of it.
bsb.12:49: The same law shall apply to both the native and the foreigner who resides among you.”
bsb.12:50: Then all the Israelites did this—they did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
bsb.12:51: And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions.
bsb.13:1: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.13:2: “Consecrate to Me every firstborn male. The firstborn from every womb among the Israelites belongs to Me, both of man and beast.”
bsb.13:3: So Moses told the people, “Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery; for the LORD brought you out of it by the strength of His hand. And nothing leavened shall be eaten.
bsb.13:4: Today, in the month of Abib, you are leaving.
bsb.13:5: And when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the land He swore to your fathers that He would give you, a land flowing with milk and honey—you shall keep this service in this month.
bsb.13:6: For seven days you are to eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the LORD.
bsb.13:7: Unleavened bread shall be eaten during those seven days. Nothing leavened may be found among you, nor shall leaven be found anywhere within your borders.
bsb.13:8: And on that day you are to explain to your son, ‘This is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’
bsb.13:9: It shall be a sign for you on your hand and a reminder on your forehead that the Law of the LORD is to be on your lips. For with a mighty hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt.
bsb.13:10: Therefore you shall keep this statute at the appointed time year after year.
bsb.13:11: And after the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as He swore to you and your fathers,
bsb.13:12: you are to present to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb. All the firstborn males of your livestock belong to the LORD.
bsb.13:13: You must redeem every firstborn donkey with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. And every firstborn of your sons you must redeem.
bsb.13:14: In the future, when your son asks you, ‘What does this mean?’ you are to tell him, ‘With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
bsb.13:15: And when Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both of man and beast. This is why I sacrifice to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb, but I redeem all the firstborn of my sons.’
bsb.13:16: So it shall serve as a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead, for with a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.”
bsb.13:17: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them along the road through the land of the Philistines, though it was shorter. For God said, “If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.”
bsb.13:18: So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea. And the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.
bsb.13:19: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear a solemn oath when he said, “God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones with you from this place.”
bsb.13:20: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham on the edge of the wilderness.
bsb.13:21: And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day, and in a pillar of fire to give them light by night, so that they could travel by day or night.
bsb.13:22: Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place before the people.
bsb.14:1: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.14:2: “Tell the Israelites to turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. You are to encamp by the sea, directly opposite Baal-zephon.
bsb.14:3: For Pharaoh will say of the Israelites, ‘They are wandering the land in confusion; the wilderness has boxed them in.’
bsb.14:4: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart so that he will pursue them. But I will gain honor by means of Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD.” So this is what the Israelites did.
bsb.14:5: When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about them and said, “What have we done? We have released Israel from serving us.”
bsb.14:6: So Pharaoh prepared his chariot and took his army with him.
bsb.14:7: He took 600 of the best chariots, and all the other chariots of Egypt, with officers over all of them.
bsb.14:8: And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt so that he pursued the Israelites, who were marching out defiantly.
bsb.14:9: The Egyptians—all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots, horsemen and troops—pursued the Israelites and overtook them as they camped by the sea near Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon.
bsb.14:10: As Pharaoh approached, the Israelites looked up and saw the Egyptians marching after them, and they were terrified and cried out to the LORD.
bsb.14:11: They said to Moses, “Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us into the wilderness to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?
bsb.14:12: Did we not say to you in Egypt, ‘Leave us alone so that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”
bsb.14:13: But Moses told the people, “Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the LORD’s salvation, which He will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians you see today, you will never see again.
bsb.14:14: The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still.”
bsb.14:15: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Why are you crying out to Me? Tell the Israelites to go forward.
bsb.14:16: And as for you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.
bsb.14:17: And I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them. Then I will gain honor by means of Pharaoh and all his army and chariots and horsemen.
bsb.14:18: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I am honored through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.”
bsb.14:19: And the angel of God, who had gone before the camp of Israel, withdrew and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them,
bsb.14:20: so that it came between the camps of Egypt and Israel. The cloud was there in the darkness, but it lit up the night. So all night long neither camp went near the other.
bsb.14:21: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind that turned it into dry land. So the waters were divided,
bsb.14:22: and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.
bsb.14:23: And the Egyptians chased after them—all Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen—and followed them into the sea.
bsb.14:24: At morning watch, however, the LORD looked down on the army of the Egyptians from the pillar of fire and cloud, and He threw their camp into confusion.
bsb.14:25: He caused their chariot wheels to wobble, so that they had difficulty driving. “Let us flee from the Israelites,” said the Egyptians, “for the LORD is fighting for them against Egypt!”
bsb.14:26: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, so that the waters may flow back over the Egyptians and their chariots and horsemen.”
bsb.14:27: So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at daybreak the sea returned to its normal state. As the Egyptians were retreating, the LORD swept them into the sea.
bsb.14:28: The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen—the entire army of Pharaoh that had chased the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.
bsb.14:29: But the Israelites had walked through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.
bsb.14:30: That day the LORD saved Israel from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore.
bsb.14:31: When Israel saw the great power that the LORD had exercised over the Egyptians, the people feared the LORD and believed in Him and in His servant Moses.
bsb.15:1: Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD: “I will sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted. The horse and rider He has thrown into the sea.
bsb.15:2: The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation. He is my God, and I will praise Him, my father’s God, and I will exalt Him.
bsb.15:3: The LORD is a warrior, the LORD is His name.
