bsb.15:4: Pharaoh’s chariots and army He has cast into the sea; the finest of his officers are drowned in the Red Sea.
bsb.15:5: The depths have covered them; they sank there like a stone.
bsb.15:6: Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic in power; Your right hand, O LORD, has shattered the enemy.
bsb.15:7: You overthrew Your adversaries by Your great majesty. You unleashed Your burning wrath; it consumed them like stubble.
bsb.15:8: At the blast of Your nostrils the waters piled up; like a wall the currents stood firm; the depths congealed in the heart of the sea.
bsb.15:9: The enemy declared, ‘I will pursue, I will overtake. I will divide the spoils; I will gorge myself on them. I will draw my sword; my hand will destroy them.’
bsb.15:10: But You blew with Your breath, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
bsb.15:11: Who among the gods is like You, O LORD? Who is like You—majestic in holiness, revered with praises, performing wonders?
bsb.15:12: You stretched out Your right hand, and the earth swallowed them up.
bsb.15:13: With loving devotion You will lead the people You have redeemed; with Your strength You will guide them to Your holy dwelling.
bsb.15:14: The nations will hear and tremble; anguish will grip the dwellers of Philistia.
bsb.15:15: Then the chiefs of Edom will be dismayed; trembling will seize the leaders of Moab; those who dwell in Canaan will melt away,
bsb.15:16: and terror and dread will fall on them. By the power of Your arm they will be as still as a stone until Your people pass by, O LORD, until the people You have bought pass by.
bsb.15:17: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance— the place, O LORD, You have prepared for Your dwelling, the sanctuary, O Lord, Your hands have established.
bsb.15:18: The LORD will reign forever and ever!”
bsb.15:19: For when Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them. But the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.
bsb.15:20: Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women followed her with tambourines and dancing.
bsb.15:21: And Miriam sang back to them: “Sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted; the horse and rider He has thrown into the sea.”
bsb.15:22: Then Moses led Israel from the Red Sea, and they went out into the Desert of Shur. For three days they walked in the desert without finding water.
bsb.15:23: And when they came to Marah, they could not drink the water there because it was bitter. (That is why it was named Marah.)
bsb.15:24: So the people grumbled against Moses, saying, “What are we to drink?”
bsb.15:25: And Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a log. And when he cast it into the waters, they were sweetened. There the LORD made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there He tested them,
bsb.15:26: saying, “If you will listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His eyes, and pay attention to His commands, and keep all His statutes, then I will not bring on you any of the diseases I inflicted on the Egyptians. For I am the LORD who heals you.”
bsb.15:27: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the waters.
bsb.16:1: On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt, the whole congregation of Israel set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.
bsb.16:2: And there in the desert they all grumbled against Moses and Aaron.
bsb.16:3: “If only we had died by the LORD’s hand in the land of Egypt!” they said. “There we sat by pots of meat and ate our fill of bread, but you have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!”
bsb.16:4: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test whether or not they will follow My instructions.
bsb.16:5: Then on the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather on the other days.”
bsb.16:6: So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, “This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt,
bsb.16:7: and in the morning you will see the LORD’s glory, because He has heard your grumbling against Him. For who are we that you should grumble against us?”
bsb.16:8: And Moses added, “The LORD will give you meat to eat this evening and bread to fill you in the morning, for He has heard your grumbling against Him. Who are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against the LORD.”
bsb.16:9: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Tell the whole congregation of Israel, ‘Come before the LORD, for He has heard your grumbling.’”
bsb.16:10: And as Aaron was speaking to the whole congregation of Israel, they looked toward the desert, and there in a cloud the glory of the LORD appeared.
bsb.16:11: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.16:12: “I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, ‘At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’”
bsb.16:13: That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
bsb.16:14: When the layer of dew had evaporated, there were thin flakes on the desert floor, as fine as frost on the ground.
bsb.16:15: When the Israelites saw it, they asked one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. So Moses told them, “It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.
bsb.16:16: This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Each one is to gather as much as he needs. You may take an omer for each person in your tent.’”
bsb.16:17: So the Israelites did this. Some gathered more, and some less.
bsb.16:18: When they measured it by the omer, he who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall. Each one gathered as much as he needed to eat.
bsb.16:19: Then Moses said to them, “No one may keep any of it until morning.”
bsb.16:20: But they did not listen to Moses; some people left part of it until morning, and it became infested with maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.
bsb.16:21: Every morning each one gathered as much as was needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
bsb.16:22: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food—two omers per person—and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported this to Moses.
bsb.16:23: He told them, “This is what the LORD has said: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil. Then set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.’”
bsb.16:24: So they set it aside until morning as Moses had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.
bsb.16:25: “Eat it today,” Moses said, “because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find anything in the field.
bsb.16:26: For six days you may gather, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, it will not be there.”
bsb.16:27: Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they did not find anything.
bsb.16:28: Then the LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?
bsb.16:29: Understand that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day He will give you bread for two days. On the seventh day, everyone must stay where he is; no one may leave his place.”
bsb.16:30: So the people rested on the seventh day.
bsb.16:31: Now the house of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
bsb.16:32: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of manna for the generations to come, so that they may see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”
bsb.16:33: So Moses told Aaron, “Take a jar and fill it with an omer of manna. Then place it before the LORD to be preserved for the generations to come.”
bsb.16:34: And Aaron placed it in front of the Testimony, to be preserved just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
bsb.16:35: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where they could settle; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
bsb.16:36: (Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.)
bsb.17:1: Then the whole congregation of Israel left the Desert of Sin, moving from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
bsb.17:2: So the people contended with Moses, “Give us water to drink.” “Why do you contend with me?” Moses replied. “Why do you test the LORD?”
bsb.17:3: But the people thirsted for water there, and they grumbled against Moses: “Why have you brought us out of Egypt—to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?”
bsb.17:4: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, “What should I do with these people? A little more and they will stone me!”
bsb.17:5: And the LORD said to Moses, “Walk on ahead of the people and take some of the elders of Israel with you. Take along in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
bsb.17:6: Behold, I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.” So Moses did this in the sight of the elders of Israel.
bsb.17:7: He named the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled, and because they tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
bsb.17:8: After this, the Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.
bsb.17:9: So Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on the hilltop with the staff of God in my hand.”
bsb.17:10: Joshua did as Moses had instructed him and fought against the Amalekites, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
bsb.17:11: As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed; but when he lowered them, Amalek prevailed.
bsb.17:12: When Moses’ hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side, so that his hands remained steady until the sun went down.
bsb.17:13: So Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his army with the sword.
bsb.17:14: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to Joshua, because I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.”
bsb.17:15: And Moses built an altar and named it The LORD Is My Banner.
bsb.17:16: “Indeed,” he said, “a hand was lifted up toward the throne of the LORD. The LORD will war against Amalek from generation to generation.”
bsb.18:1: Now Moses’ father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, heard about all that God had done for Moses and His people Israel, and how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
bsb.18:2: After Moses had sent back his wife Zipporah, his father-in-law Jethro had received her,
bsb.18:3: along with her two sons. One son was named Gershom, for Moses had said, “I have been a foreigner in a foreign land.”
bsb.18:4: The other son was named Eliezer, for Moses had said, “The God of my father was my helper and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.”
bsb.18:5: Moses’ father-in-law Jethro, along with Moses’ wife and sons, came to him in the desert, where he was encamped at the mountain of God.
bsb.18:6: He sent word to Moses, “I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons.”
bsb.18:7: So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law and bowed down and kissed him. They greeted each other and went into the tent.
bsb.18:8: Then Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the hardships they had encountered along the way, and how the LORD had delivered them.
bsb.18:9: And Jethro rejoiced over all the good things the LORD had done for Israel, whom He had rescued from the hand of the Egyptians.
bsb.18:10: Jethro declared, “Blessed be the LORD, who has delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and of Pharaoh, and who has delivered the people from the hand of the Egyptians.
bsb.18:11: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, for He did this when they treated Israel with arrogance.”
bsb.18:12: Then Moses’ father-in-law Jethro brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law in the presence of God.
bsb.18:13: The next day Moses took his seat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.
bsb.18:14: When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he asked, “What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone as judge, with all the people standing around you from morning till evening?”
bsb.18:15: “Because the people come to me to inquire of God,” Moses replied.
bsb.18:16: “Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me to judge between one man and another, and I make known to them the statutes and laws of God.”
bsb.18:17: But Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “What you are doing is not good.
bsb.18:18: Surely you and these people with you will wear yourselves out, because the task is too heavy for you. You cannot handle it alone.
bsb.18:19: Now listen to me; I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must be the people’s representative before God and bring their causes to Him.
bsb.18:20: Teach them the statutes and laws, and show them the way to live and the work they must do.
bsb.18:21: Furthermore, select capable men from among the people—God-fearing, trustworthy men who are averse to dishonest gain. Appoint them over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
bsb.18:22: Have these men judge the people at all times. Then they can bring you any major issue, but all minor cases they can judge on their own, so that your load may be lightened as they share it with you.
bsb.18:23: If you follow this advice and God so directs you, then you will be able to endure, and all these people can go home in peace.”
bsb.18:24: Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
bsb.18:25: So Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
bsb.18:26: And they judged the people at all times; they would bring the difficult cases to Moses, but any minor issue they would judge themselves.
bsb.18:27: Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and Jethro returned to his own land.
bsb.19:1: In the third month, on the same day of the month that the Israelites had left the land of Egypt, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai.
bsb.19:2: After they had set out from Rephidim, they entered the Wilderness of Sinai, and Israel camped there in front of the mountain.
bsb.19:3: Then Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, “This is what you are to tell the house of Jacob and explain to the sons of Israel:
bsb.19:4: ‘You have seen for yourselves what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself.
bsb.19:5: Now if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, you will be My treasured possession out of all the nations—for the whole earth is Mine.
bsb.19:6: And unto Me you shall be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words that you are to speak to the Israelites.”
bsb.19:7: So Moses went back and summoned the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
bsb.19:8: And all the people answered together, “We will do everything that the LORD has spoken.” So Moses brought their words back to the LORD.
bsb.19:9: The LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you, and they will always put their trust in you.” And Moses relayed to the LORD what the people had said.
bsb.19:10: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. They must wash their clothes
bsb.19:11: and be prepared by the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
bsb.19:12: And you are to set up a boundary for the people around the mountain and tell them, ‘Be careful not to go up on the mountain or touch its base. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.
bsb.19:13: No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot with arrows—whether man or beast, he must not live.’ Only when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast may they approach the mountain.”
bsb.19:14: When Moses came down from the mountain to the people, he consecrated them, and they washed their clothes.
bsb.19:15: “Be prepared for the third day,” he said to the people. “Do not draw near to a woman.”
bsb.19:16: On the third day, when morning came, there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud was upon the mountain, and a very loud blast of the ram’s horn went out, so that all the people in the camp trembled.
bsb.19:17: Then Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
bsb.19:18: Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke, because the LORD had descended on it in fire. And the smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked violently.
bsb.19:19: And as the sound of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him in the thunder.
bsb.19:20: The LORD descended to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the summit. So Moses went up,
bsb.19:21: and the LORD said to him, “Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish.
bsb.19:22: Even the priests who approach the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them.”
bsb.19:23: But Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for You solemnly warned us, ‘Put a boundary around the mountain and set it apart as holy.’”
bsb.19:24: And the LORD replied, “Go down and bring Aaron with you. But the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or He will break out against them.”
bsb.19:25: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
bsb.20:1: And God spoke all these words:
bsb.20:2: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
bsb.20:3: You shall have no other gods before Me.
bsb.20:4: You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.
bsb.20:5: You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
bsb.20:6: but showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments.
bsb.20:7: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.
bsb.20:8: Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.
bsb.20:9: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
bsb.20:10: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God, on which you must not do any work—neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant or livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates.
bsb.20:11: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in them, but on the seventh day He rested. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy.
bsb.20:12: Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
bsb.20:16: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
bsb.20:17: You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his manservant or maidservant, or his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”
bsb.20:18: When all the people witnessed the thunder and lightning, the sounding of the ram’s horn, and the mountain enveloped in smoke, they trembled and stood at a distance.
bsb.20:19: “Speak to us yourself and we will listen,” they said to Moses. “But do not let God speak to us, or we will die.”
bsb.20:20: “Do not be afraid,” Moses replied. “For God has come to test you, so that the fear of Him may be before you, to keep you from sinning.”
bsb.20:21: And the people stood at a distance as Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.
bsb.20:22: Then the LORD said to Moses, “This is what you are to tell the Israelites: ‘You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven.
bsb.20:23: You are not to make any gods alongside Me; you are not to make for yourselves gods of silver or gold.
bsb.20:24: You are to make for Me an altar of earth, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and goats and cattle. In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
bsb.20:25: Now if you make an altar of stones for Me, you must not build it with stones shaped by tools; for if you use a chisel on it, you will defile it.
bsb.20:26: And you must not go up to My altar on steps, lest your nakedness be exposed on it.’
bsb.21:1: “These are the ordinances that you are to set before them:
bsb.21:2: If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free without paying anything.
bsb.21:3: If he arrived alone, he is to leave alone; if he arrived with a wife, she is to leave with him.
bsb.21:4: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and only the man shall go free.
bsb.21:5: But if the servant declares, ‘I love my master and my wife and children; I do not want to go free,’
bsb.21:6: then his master is to bring him before the judges. And he shall take him to the door or doorpost and pierce his ear with an awl. Then he shall serve his master for life.
bsb.21:7: And if a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free as the menservants do.
bsb.21:8: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who had designated her for himself, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, since he has broken faith with her.
bsb.21:9: And if he chooses her for his son, he must deal with her as with a daughter.
bsb.21:10: If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the food, clothing, or marital rights of his first wife.
bsb.21:11: If, however, he does not provide her with these three things, she is free to go without monetary payment.
bsb.21:12: Whoever strikes and kills a man must surely be put to death.
bsb.21:13: If, however, he did not lie in wait, but God allowed it to happen, then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.
bsb.21:14: But if a man schemes and acts willfully against his neighbor to kill him, you must take him away from My altar to be put to death.
bsb.21:15: Whoever strikes his father or mother must surely be put to death.
bsb.21:16: Whoever kidnaps another man must be put to death, whether he sells him or the man is found in his possession.
bsb.21:17: Anyone who curses his father or mother must surely be put to death.
bsb.21:18: If men are quarreling and one strikes the other with a stone or a fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed,
bsb.21:19: then the one who struck him shall go unpunished, as long as the other can get up and walk around outside with his staff. Nevertheless, he must compensate the man for his lost work and see that he is completely healed.
bsb.21:20: If a man strikes his manservant or maidservant with a rod, and the servant dies by his hand, he shall surely be punished.
bsb.21:21: However, if the servant gets up after a day or two, the owner shall not be punished, since the servant is his property.
bsb.21:22: If men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, he shall surely be fined as the woman’s husband demands and as the court allows.
bsb.21:23: But if a serious injury results, then you must require a life for a life—
bsb.21:24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
bsb.21:25: burn for burn, wound for wound, and stripe for stripe.
bsb.21:26: If a man strikes and blinds the eye of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the eye.
bsb.21:27: And if he knocks out the tooth of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the tooth.
bsb.21:28: If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must surely be stoned, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the ox shall not be held responsible.
bsb.21:29: But if the ox has a habit of goring, and its owner has been warned yet does not restrain it, and it kills a man or woman, then the ox must be stoned and its owner must also be put to death.
bsb.21:30: If payment is demanded of him instead, he may redeem his life by paying the full amount demanded of him.
bsb.21:31: If the ox gores a son or a daughter, it shall be done to him according to the same rule.
bsb.21:32: If the ox gores a manservant or maidservant, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver to the master of that servant, and the ox must be stoned.
bsb.21:33: If a man opens or digs a pit and fails to cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
bsb.21:34: the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he must pay its owner, and the dead animal will be his.
bsb.21:35: If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they must sell the live one and divide the proceeds; they also must divide the dead animal.
bsb.21:36: But if it was known that the ox had a habit of goring, yet its owner failed to restrain it, he shall pay full compensation, ox for ox, and the dead animal will be his.
bsb.22:1: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters or sells it, he must repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.
bsb.22:2: If a thief is caught breaking in and is beaten to death, no one shall be guilty of bloodshed.
bsb.22:3: But if it happens after sunrise, there is guilt for his bloodshed. A thief must make full restitution; if he has nothing, he himself shall be sold for his theft.
bsb.22:4: If what was stolen is actually found alive in his possession—whether ox or donkey or sheep—he must pay back double.
bsb.22:5: If a man grazes his livestock in a field or vineyard and allows them to stray so that they graze in someone else’s field, he must make restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard.
bsb.22:6: If a fire breaks out and spreads to thornbushes so that it consumes stacked or standing grain, or the whole field, the one who started the fire must make full restitution.
bsb.22:7: If a man gives his neighbor money or goods for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house, the thief, if caught, must pay back double.
bsb.22:8: If the thief is not found, the owner of the house must appear before the judges to determine whether he has taken his neighbor’s property.
bsb.22:9: In all cases of illegal possession of an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item that someone claims, ‘This is mine,’ both parties shall bring their cases before the judges. The one whom the judges find guilty must pay back double to his neighbor.
bsb.22:10: If a man gives a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to be cared for by his neighbor, but it dies or is injured or stolen while no one is watching,
bsb.22:11: an oath before the LORD shall be made between the parties to determine whether or not the man has taken his neighbor’s property. The owner must accept the oath and require no restitution.
bsb.22:12: But if the animal was actually stolen from the neighbor, he must make restitution to the owner.
bsb.22:13: If the animal was torn to pieces, he shall bring it as evidence; he need not make restitution for the torn carcass.
bsb.22:14: If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is injured or dies while its owner is not present, he must make full restitution.
bsb.22:15: If the owner was present, no restitution is required. If the animal was rented, the fee covers the loss.
bsb.22:16: If a man seduces a virgin who is not pledged in marriage and sleeps with her, he must pay the full dowry for her to be his wife.
bsb.22:17: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, the man still must pay an amount comparable to the bridal price of a virgin.
bsb.22:18: You must not allow a sorceress to live.
bsb.22:19: Whoever lies with an animal must surely be put to death.
bsb.22:20: If anyone sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone, he must be set apart for destruction.
bsb.22:21: You must not exploit or oppress a foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
bsb.22:22: You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.
bsb.22:23: If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to Me in distress, I will surely hear their cry.
bsb.22:24: My anger will be kindled, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives will become widows and your children will be fatherless.
bsb.22:25: If you lend money to one of My people among you who is poor, you must not act as a creditor to him; you are not to charge him interest.
bsb.22:26: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him by sunset,
bsb.22:27: because his cloak is the only covering he has for his body. What else will he sleep in? And if he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.
bsb.22:28: You must not blaspheme God or curse the ruler of your people.
bsb.22:29: You must not hold back offerings from your granaries or vats. You are to give Me the firstborn of your sons.
bsb.22:30: You shall do likewise with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day you are to give them to Me.
bsb.22:31: You are to be My holy people. You must not eat the meat of a mauled animal found in the field; you are to throw it to the dogs.
bsb.23:1: “You shall not spread a false report. Do not join the wicked by being a malicious witness.
bsb.23:2: You shall not follow the crowd in wrongdoing. When you testify in a lawsuit, do not pervert justice by siding with the crowd.
bsb.23:3: And do not show favoritism to a poor man in his lawsuit.
bsb.23:4: If you encounter your enemy’s stray ox or donkey, you must return it to him.
bsb.23:5: If you see the donkey of one who hates you fallen under its load, do not leave it there; you must help him with it.
bsb.23:6: You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.
bsb.23:7: Stay far away from a false accusation. Do not kill the innocent or the just, for I will not acquit the guilty.
bsb.23:8: Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.
bsb.23:9: Do not oppress a foreign resident, since you yourselves know how it feels to be foreigners; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
bsb.23:10: For six years you are to sow your land and gather its produce,
bsb.23:11: but in the seventh year you must let it rest and lie fallow, so that the poor among your people may eat from the field and the wild animals may consume what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and olive grove.
bsb.23:12: For six days you are to do your work, but on the seventh day you must cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest and the son of your maidservant may be refreshed, as well as the foreign resident.
bsb.23:13: Pay close attention to everything I have said to you. You must not invoke the names of other gods; they must not be heard on your lips.
bsb.23:14: Three times a year you are to celebrate a feast to Me.
bsb.23:15: You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread as I commanded you: At the appointed time in the month of Abib you are to eat unleavened bread for seven days, because that was the month you came out of Egypt. No one may appear before Me empty-handed.
bsb.23:16: You are also to keep the Feast of Harvest with the firstfruits of the produce from what you sow in the field. And keep the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather your produce from the field.
bsb.23:17: Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD.
bsb.23:18: You must not offer the blood of My sacrifices with anything leavened, nor may the fat of My feast remain until morning.
bsb.23:19: Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
bsb.23:20: Behold, I am sending an angel before you to protect you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
bsb.23:21: Pay attention to him and listen to his voice; do not defy him, for he will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.
bsb.23:22: But if you will listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.
bsb.23:23: For My angel will go before you and bring you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will annihilate them.
bsb.23:24: You must not bow down to their gods or serve them or follow their practices. Instead, you are to demolish them and smash their sacred stones to pieces.
bsb.23:25: So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. And I will take away sickness from among you.
bsb.23:26: No woman in your land will miscarry or be barren; I will fulfill the number of your days.
bsb.23:27: I will send My terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn and run.
bsb.23:28: I will send the hornet before you to drive the Hivites and Canaanites and Hittites out of your way.
bsb.23:29: I will not drive them out before you in a single year; otherwise the land would become desolate and wild animals would multiply against you.
bsb.23:30: Little by little I will drive them out ahead of you, until you become fruitful and possess the land.
bsb.23:31: And I will establish your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates. For I will deliver the inhabitants into your hand, and you will drive them out before you.
bsb.23:32: You shall make no covenant with them or with their gods.
bsb.23:33: They must not remain in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me. For if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”
bsb.24:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD—you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders—and you are to worship at a distance.
bsb.24:2: Moses alone shall approach the LORD, but the others must not come near. And the people may not go up with him.”
bsb.24:3: When Moses came and told the people all the words and ordinances of the LORD, they all responded with one voice: “All the words that the LORD has spoken, we will do.”
bsb.24:4: And Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. Early the next morning he got up and built an altar at the base of the mountain, along with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
bsb.24:5: Then he sent out some young men of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.
bsb.24:6: Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and the other half he sprinkled on the altar.
bsb.24:7: Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it to the people, who replied, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will be obedient.”
bsb.24:8: So Moses took the blood, sprinkled it on the people, and said, “This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
bsb.24:9: Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel,
bsb.24:10: and they saw the God of Israel. Under His feet was a work like a pavement made of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.
bsb.24:11: But God did not lay His hand on the nobles of Israel; they saw Him, and they ate and drank.
bsb.24:12: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to Me on the mountain and stay here, so that I may give you the tablets of stone, with the law and commandments I have written for their instruction.”
bsb.24:13: So Moses set out with Joshua his attendant and went up on the mountain of God.
bsb.24:14: And he said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are here with you. Whoever has a dispute can go to them.”
bsb.24:15: When Moses went up on the mountain, the cloud covered it,
bsb.24:16: and the glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai. For six days the cloud covered it, and on the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from within the cloud.
bsb.24:17: And the sight of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the mountaintop in the eyes of the Israelites.
bsb.24:18: Moses entered the cloud as he went up on the mountain, and he remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
bsb.25:1: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.25:2: “Tell the Israelites to bring Me an offering. You are to receive My offering from every man whose heart compels him.
bsb.25:3: This is the offering you are to accept from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
bsb.25:4: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goat hair;
bsb.25:5: ram skins dyed red and fine leather; acacia wood;
bsb.25:6: olive oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
bsb.25:7: and onyx stones and gemstones to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.
bsb.25:8: And they are to make a sanctuary for Me, so that I may dwell among them.
bsb.25:9: You must make the tabernacle and design all its furnishings according to the pattern I show you.
bsb.25:10: And they are to construct an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
bsb.25:11: Overlay it with pure gold both inside and out, and make a gold molding around it.
bsb.25:12: Cast four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.
bsb.25:13: And make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
bsb.25:14: Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, in order to carry it.
bsb.25:15: The poles are to remain in the rings of the ark; they must not be removed.
bsb.25:16: And place inside the ark the Testimony, which I will give you.
bsb.25:17: And you are to construct a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
bsb.25:18: Make two cherubim of hammered gold at the ends of the mercy seat,
bsb.25:19: one cherub on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold.
bsb.25:20: And the cherubim are to have wings that spread upward, overshadowing the mercy seat. The cherubim are to face each other, looking toward the mercy seat.
bsb.25:21: Set the mercy seat atop the ark, and put the Testimony that I will give you into the ark.
bsb.25:22: And I will meet with you there above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the Testimony; I will speak with you about all that I command you regarding the Israelites.
bsb.25:23: You are also to make a table of acacia wood two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
bsb.25:24: Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold molding around it.
bsb.25:25: And make a rim around it a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim.
bsb.25:26: Make four gold rings for the table and fasten them to the four corners at its four legs.
bsb.25:27: The rings are to be close to the rim, to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
bsb.25:28: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, so that the table may be carried with them.
bsb.25:29: You are also to make the plates and dishes, as well as the pitchers and bowls for pouring drink offerings. Make them out of pure gold.
bsb.25:30: And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times.
bsb.25:31: Then you are to make a lampstand of pure, hammered gold. It shall be made of one piece, including its base and shaft, its cups, and its buds and petals.
bsb.25:32: Six branches are to extend from the sides of the lampstand—three on one side and three on the other.
bsb.25:33: There are to be three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the first branch, each with buds and petals, three on the next branch, and the same for all six branches that extend from the lampstand.
bsb.25:34: And on the lampstand there shall be four cups shaped like almond blossoms with buds and petals.
bsb.25:35: For the six branches that extend from the lampstand, a bud must be under the first pair of branches, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair.
bsb.25:36: The buds and branches are to be all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
bsb.25:37: Make seven lamps and set them up on the lampstand so that they illuminate the area in front of it.
bsb.25:38: The wick trimmers and their trays must be of pure gold.
bsb.25:39: The lampstand and all these utensils shall be made from a talent of pure gold.
bsb.25:40: See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.
bsb.26:1: “You are to construct the tabernacle itself with ten curtains of finely spun linen, each with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and cherubim skillfully worked into them.
bsb.26:2: Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide—all curtains the same size.
bsb.26:3: Five of the curtains are to be joined together, and the other five joined as well.
bsb.26:4: Make loops of blue material on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same for the end curtain in the second set.
bsb.26:5: Make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, so that the loops line up opposite one another.
bsb.26:6: Make fifty gold clasps as well, and join the curtains together with the clasps, so that the tabernacle will be a unit.
bsb.26:7: You are to make curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle—eleven curtains in all.
bsb.26:8: Each of the eleven curtains is to be the same size—thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.
bsb.26:9: Join five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another. Then fold the sixth curtain over double at the front of the tent.
bsb.26:10: Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the corresponding curtain in the second set.
bsb.26:11: Make fifty bronze clasps and put them through the loops to join the tent together as a unit.
bsb.26:12: As for the overlap that remains of the tent curtains, the half curtain that is left over shall hang down over the back of the tabernacle.
bsb.26:13: And the tent curtains will be a cubit longer on either side, and the excess will hang over the sides of the tabernacle to cover it.
bsb.26:14: Also make a covering for the tent out of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
bsb.26:15: You are to construct upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
bsb.26:16: Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
bsb.26:17: Two tenons must be connected to each other for each frame. Make all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.
bsb.26:18: Construct twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle,
bsb.26:19: with forty silver bases under the twenty frames—two bases for each frame, one under each tenon.
bsb.26:20: For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, make twenty frames
bsb.26:21: and forty silver bases—two bases under each frame.
bsb.26:22: Make six frames for the rear of the tabernacle, the west side,
bsb.26:23: and two frames for the two back corners of the tabernacle,
bsb.26:24: coupled together from bottom to top and fitted into a single ring. These will serve as the two corners.
bsb.26:25: So there are to be eight frames and sixteen silver bases—two under each frame.
bsb.26:26: You are also to make five crossbars of acacia wood for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
bsb.26:27: five for those on the other side, and five for those on the rear side of the tabernacle, to the west.
bsb.26:28: The central crossbar in the middle of the frames shall extend from one end to the other.
bsb.26:29: Overlay the frames with gold and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Also overlay the crossbars with gold.
bsb.26:30: So you are to set up the tabernacle according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.
bsb.26:31: Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it.
bsb.26:32: Hang it with gold hooks on four posts of acacia wood, overlaid with gold and standing on four silver bases.
bsb.26:33: And hang the veil from the clasps and place the ark of the Testimony behind the veil. So the veil will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
bsb.26:34: Put the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy Place.
bsb.26:35: And place the table outside the veil on the north side of the tabernacle, and put the lampstand opposite the table, on the south side.
bsb.26:36: For the entrance to the tent, you are to make a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen.
bsb.26:37: Make five posts of acacia wood for the curtain, overlay them with gold hooks, and cast five bronze bases for them.
bsb.27:1: “You are to build an altar of acacia wood. The altar must be square, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
bsb.27:2: Make a horn on each of its four corners, so that the horns are of one piece, and overlay it with bronze.
bsb.27:3: Make all its utensils of bronze—its pots for removing ashes, its shovels, its sprinkling bowls, its meat forks, and its firepans.
bsb.27:4: Construct for it a grate of bronze mesh, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the mesh.
bsb.27:5: Set the grate beneath the ledge of the altar, so that the mesh comes halfway up the altar.
bsb.27:6: Additionally, make poles of acacia wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.
bsb.27:7: The poles are to be inserted into the rings so that the poles are on two sides of the altar when it is carried.
bsb.27:8: Construct the altar with boards so that it is hollow. It is to be made just as you were shown on the mountain.
bsb.27:9: You are also to make a courtyard for the tabernacle. On the south side of the courtyard make curtains of finely spun linen, a hundred cubits long on one side,
bsb.27:10: with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.
bsb.27:11: Likewise there are to be curtains on the north side, a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
bsb.27:12: The curtains on the west side of the courtyard shall be fifty cubits wide, with ten posts and ten bases.
bsb.27:13: The east side of the courtyard, toward the sunrise, is to be fifty cubits wide.
bsb.27:14: Make the curtains on one side fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,
bsb.27:15: and the curtains on the other side fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
bsb.27:16: The gate of the courtyard shall be twenty cubits long, with a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. It shall have four posts and four bases.
bsb.27:17: All the posts around the courtyard shall have silver bands, silver hooks, and bronze bases.
bsb.27:18: The entire courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with curtains of finely spun linen five cubits high, and with bronze bases.
bsb.27:19: All the utensils of the tabernacle for every use, including all its tent pegs and the tent pegs of the courtyard, shall be made of bronze.
bsb.27:20: And you are to command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually.
bsb.27:21: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil that is in front of the Testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamps before the LORD from evening until morning. This is to be a permanent statute for the Israelites for the generations to come.
bsb.28:1: “Next, have your brother Aaron brought to you from among the Israelites, along with his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, to serve Me as priests.
bsb.28:2: Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, to give him glory and splendor.
bsb.28:3: You are to instruct all the skilled craftsmen, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, to make garments for Aaron’s consecration, so that he may serve Me as priest.
bsb.28:4: These are the garments that they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. They are to make these holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they may serve Me as priests.
bsb.28:5: They shall use gold, along with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
bsb.28:6: They are to make the ephod of finely spun linen embroidered with gold, and with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
bsb.28:7: It shall have two shoulder pieces attached at two of its corners, so it can be fastened.
bsb.28:8: And the skillfully woven waistband of the ephod must be of one piece, of the same workmanship—with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen.
bsb.28:9: Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
bsb.28:10: six of their names on one stone and the remaining six on the other, in the order of their birth.
bsb.28:11: Engrave the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a gem cutter engraves a seal. Then mount the stones in gold filigree settings.
bsb.28:12: Fasten both stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Aaron is to bear their names on his two shoulders as a memorial before the LORD.
bsb.28:14: and two chains of pure gold, made of braided cord work; and attach these chains to the settings.
bsb.28:15: You are also to make a breastpiece of judgment with the same workmanship as the ephod. Construct it with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen.
bsb.28:16: It must be square when folded over double, a span long and a span wide.
bsb.28:17: And mount on it a setting of gemstones, four rows of stones: In the first row there shall be a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald;
bsb.28:18: in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
bsb.28:19: in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
bsb.28:20: and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount these stones in gold filigree settings.
bsb.28:21: The twelve stones are to correspond to the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
bsb.28:22: For the breastpiece, make braided chains like cords of pure gold.
bsb.28:23: You are also to make two gold rings and fasten them to the two corners of the breastpiece.
bsb.28:24: Then fasten the two gold chains to the two gold rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
bsb.28:25: and fasten the other ends of the two chains to the two filigree settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
bsb.28:26: Make two more gold rings and attach them to the other two corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
bsb.28:27: Make two additional gold rings and attach them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on its front, near its seam just above its woven waistband.
bsb.28:28: The rings of the breastpiece shall be tied to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn, so that the breastpiece is above the waistband of the ephod and does not swing out from the ephod.
bsb.28:29: Whenever Aaron enters the Holy Place, he shall bear the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece of judgment, as a continual reminder before the LORD.
bsb.28:30: And place the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece of judgment, so that they will also be over Aaron’s heart whenever he comes before the LORD. Aaron will continually carry the judgment of the sons of Israel over his heart before the LORD.
bsb.28:31: You are to make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth,
bsb.28:32: with an opening at its top in the center. Around the opening shall be a woven collar with an opening like that of a garment, so that it will not tear.
bsb.28:33: Make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn all the way around the lower hem, with gold bells between them,
bsb.28:34: alternating the gold bells and pomegranates around the lower hem of the robe.
bsb.28:35: Aaron must wear the robe whenever he ministers, and its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD, so that he will not die.
bsb.28:36: You are to make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it as on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
bsb.28:37: Fasten to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban.
bsb.28:38: And it will be worn on Aaron’s forehead, so that he may bear the iniquity of the holy things that the sons of Israel consecrate with regard to all their holy gifts. It shall always be on his forehead, so that they may be acceptable before the LORD.
bsb.28:39: You are to weave the tunic with fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and fashion an embroidered sash.
bsb.28:40: Make tunics, sashes, and headbands for Aaron’s sons, to give them glory and splendor.
bsb.28:41: After you put these garments on your brother Aaron and his sons, anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them so that they may serve Me as priests.
bsb.28:42: Make linen undergarments to cover their bare flesh, extending from waist to thigh.
bsb.28:43: Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they will not incur guilt and die. This is to be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants.
bsb.29:1: “Now this is what you are to do to consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests: Take a young bull and two rams without blemish,
bsb.29:2: along with unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil. Make them out of fine wheat flour,
bsb.29:3: put them in a basket, and present them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
bsb.29:4: Then present Aaron and his sons at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
bsb.29:5: Take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, and the breastplate. Fasten the ephod on him with its woven waistband.
bsb.29:6: Put the turban on his head and attach the holy diadem to the turban.
bsb.29:7: Then take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head.
bsb.29:8: Present his sons as well and clothe them with tunics.
bsb.29:9: Wrap the sashes around Aaron and his sons and tie headbands on them. The priesthood shall be theirs by a permanent statute. In this way you are to ordain Aaron and his sons.
bsb.29:10: You are to present the bull at the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.
bsb.29:11: And you shall slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
bsb.29:12: Take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger; then pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
bsb.29:13: Take all the fat that covers the entrails and the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
bsb.29:14: But burn the flesh of the bull and its hide and dung outside the camp; it is a sin offering.
bsb.29:15: Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
bsb.29:16: You are to slaughter the ram, take its blood, and sprinkle it on all sides of the altar.
bsb.29:17: Cut the ram into pieces, wash the entrails and legs, and place them with its head and other pieces.
bsb.29:18: Then burn the entire ram on the altar; it is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
bsb.29:19: Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.
bsb.29:20: Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Sprinkle the remaining blood on all sides of the altar.
bsb.29:21: And take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, as well as on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments will be consecrated, as well as his sons and their garments.
bsb.29:22: Take the fat from the ram, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh (since this is a ram for ordination),
bsb.29:23: along with one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
bsb.29:24: Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.
bsb.29:25: Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar atop the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma before the LORD; it is an offering made by fire to the LORD.
bsb.29:26: Take the breast of the ram of Aaron’s ordination and wave it before the LORD as a wave offering, and it will be your portion.
bsb.29:27: Consecrate for Aaron and his sons the breast of the wave offering that is waved and the thigh of the heave offering that is lifted up from the ram of ordination.
bsb.29:28: This will belong to Aaron and his sons as a regular portion from the Israelites, for it is the heave offering the Israelites will make to the LORD from their peace offerings.
bsb.29:29: The holy garments that belong to Aaron will belong to his sons after him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them.
bsb.29:30: The son who succeeds him as priest and enters the Tent of Meeting to minister in the Holy Place must wear them for seven days.
bsb.29:31: You are to take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.
bsb.29:32: At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.
bsb.29:33: They must eat those things by which atonement was made for their ordination and consecration. But no outsider may eat them, because these things are sacred.
bsb.29:34: And if any of the meat of ordination or any bread is left until the morning, you are to burn up the remainder. It must not be eaten, because it is sacred.
bsb.29:35: This is what you are to do for Aaron and his sons based on all that I have commanded you, taking seven days to ordain them.
bsb.29:36: Sacrifice a bull as a sin offering each day for atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
bsb.29:37: For seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will become most holy; whatever touches the altar will be holy.
bsb.29:38: This is what you are to offer regularly on the altar, each day: two lambs that are a year old.
bsb.29:39: Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight.
bsb.29:40: With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, mixed with a quarter hin of oil from pressed olives, and a drink offering of a quarter hin of wine.
bsb.29:41: And offer the second lamb at twilight with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
bsb.29:42: For the generations to come, this burnt offering shall be made regularly at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, where I will meet you to speak with you.
bsb.29:43: I will also meet with the Israelites there, and that place will be consecrated by My glory.
bsb.29:44: So I will consecrate the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
bsb.29:45: Then I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.
bsb.29:46: And they will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might dwell among them. I am the LORD their God.
bsb.30:1: “You are also to make an altar of acacia wood for the burning of incense.
bsb.30:2: It is to be square, a cubit long, a cubit wide, and two cubits high. Its horns must be of one piece.
bsb.30:3: Overlay with pure gold the top and all the sides and horns, and make a molding of gold around it.
bsb.30:4: And make two gold rings below the molding on opposite sides to hold the poles used to carry it.
bsb.30:5: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
bsb.30:6: Place the altar in front of the veil that is before the ark of the Testimony—before the mercy seat that is over the Testimony—where I will meet with you.
bsb.30:7: And Aaron is to burn fragrant incense on it every morning when he tends the lamps.
bsb.30:8: When Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he must burn the incense perpetually before the LORD for the generations to come.
bsb.30:9: On this altar you must not offer unauthorized incense or a burnt offering or grain offering; nor are you to pour a drink offering on it.
bsb.30:10: Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on the horns of the altar. Throughout your generations he shall make atonement on it annually with the blood of the sin offering of atonement. The altar is most holy to the LORD.”
bsb.30:11: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.30:12: “When you take a census of the Israelites to number them, each man must pay the LORD a ransom for his life when he is counted. Then no plague will come upon them when they are numbered.
bsb.30:13: Everyone who crosses over to those counted must pay a half shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, which weighs twenty gerahs. This half shekel is an offering to the LORD.
bsb.30:14: Everyone twenty years of age or older who crosses over must give this offering to the LORD.
bsb.30:15: In making the offering to the LORD to atone for your lives, the rich shall not give more than a half shekel, nor shall the poor give less.
bsb.30:16: Take the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the service of the Tent of Meeting. It will serve as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD to make atonement for your lives.”
bsb.30:17: And the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.30:18: “You are to make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. Set it between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water in it,
bsb.30:19: with which Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and feet.
bsb.30:20: Whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to minister by presenting an offering made by fire to the LORD, they must wash with water so that they will not die.
bsb.30:21: Thus they are to wash their hands and feet so that they will not die; this shall be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants for the generations to come.”
bsb.30:22: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.30:23: “Take the finest spices: 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, half that amount (250 shekels) of fragrant cinnamon, 250 shekels of fragrant cane,
bsb.30:24: 500 shekels of cassia—all according to the sanctuary shekel—and a hin of olive oil.
bsb.30:25: Prepare from these a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer; it will be a sacred anointing oil.
bsb.30:26: Use this oil to anoint the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the Testimony,
bsb.30:27: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,
bsb.30:28: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
bsb.30:29: You are to consecrate them so that they will be most holy. Whatever touches them shall be holy.
bsb.30:30: Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.
bsb.30:31: And you are to tell the Israelites, ‘This will be My sacred anointing oil for the generations to come.
bsb.30:32: It must not be used to anoint an ordinary man, and you must not make anything like it with the same formula. It is holy, and it must be holy to you.
bsb.30:33: Anyone who mixes perfume like it or puts it on an outsider shall be cut off from his people.’”
bsb.30:34: The LORD also said to Moses, “Take fragrant spices—gum resin, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense—in equal measures,
bsb.30:35: and make a fragrant blend of incense, the work of a perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
bsb.30:36: Grind some of it into fine powder and place it in front of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you.
bsb.30:37: You are never to use this formula to make incense for yourselves; you shall regard it as holy to the LORD.
bsb.30:38: Anyone who makes something like it to enjoy its fragrance shall be cut off from his people.”
bsb.31:1: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.31:2: “See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
bsb.31:3: And I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship,
bsb.31:4: to design artistic works in gold, silver, and bronze,
bsb.31:5: to cut gemstones for settings, and to carve wood, so that he may be a master of every craft.
bsb.31:6: Moreover, I have selected Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, as his assistant. I have also given skill to all the craftsmen, that they may fashion all that I have commanded you:
bsb.31:7: the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the Testimony and the mercy seat upon it, and all the other furnishings of the tent—
bsb.31:8: the table with its utensils, the pure gold lampstand with all its utensils, the altar of incense,
bsb.31:9: the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand—
bsb.31:10: as well as the woven garments, both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests,
bsb.31:11: in addition to the anointing oil and fragrant incense for the Holy Place. They are to make them according to all that I have commanded you.”
bsb.31:12: And the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.31:13: “Tell the Israelites, ‘Surely you must keep My Sabbaths, for this will be a sign between Me and you for the generations to come, so that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you.
bsb.31:14: Keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you. Anyone who profanes it must surely be put to death. Whoever does any work on that day must be cut off from among his people.
bsb.31:15: For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does any work on the Sabbath day must surely be put to death.
bsb.31:16: The Israelites must keep the Sabbath, celebrating it as a permanent covenant for the generations to come.
bsb.31:17: It is a sign between Me and the Israelites forever; for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, but on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.’”
bsb.31:18: When the LORD had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gave him the two tablets of the Testimony, tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God.
bsb.32:1: Now when the people saw that Moses was delayed in coming down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, “Come, make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him!”
bsb.32:2: So Aaron told them, “Take off the gold earrings that are on your wives and sons and daughters, and bring them to me.”
bsb.32:3: Then all the people took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.
bsb.32:4: He took the gold from their hands, and with an engraving tool he fashioned it into a molten calf. And they said, “These, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!”
bsb.32:5: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before the calf and proclaimed: “Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD.”
bsb.32:6: So the next day they arose, offered burnt offerings, and presented peace offerings. And the people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.
bsb.32:7: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go down at once, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.
bsb.32:8: How quickly they have turned aside from the way that I commanded them! They have made for themselves a molten calf and have bowed down to it. They have sacrificed to it and said, ‘These, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.’”
bsb.32:9: The LORD also said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stiff-necked people.
bsb.32:10: Now leave Me alone, so that My anger may burn against them and consume them. Then I will make you into a great nation.”
bsb.32:11: But Moses sought the favor of the LORD his God, saying, “O LORD, why does Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?
bsb.32:12: Why should the Egyptians declare, ‘He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them from the face of the earth’? Turn from Your fierce anger and relent from doing harm to Your people.
bsb.32:13: Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom You swore by Your very self when You declared, ‘I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all this land that I have promised, and it shall be their inheritance forever.’”
bsb.32:14: So the LORD relented from the calamity He had threatened to bring on His people.
bsb.32:15: Then Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands. They were inscribed on both sides, front and back.
bsb.32:16: The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
bsb.32:17: When Joshua heard the sound of the people shouting, he said to Moses, “The sound of war is in the camp.”
bsb.32:18: But Moses replied: “It is neither the cry of victory nor the cry of defeat; I hear the sound of singing!”
bsb.32:19: As Moses approached the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, he burned with anger and threw the tablets out of his hands, shattering them at the base of the mountain.
bsb.32:20: Then he took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, and scattered the powder over the face of the water. Then he forced the Israelites to drink it.
bsb.32:21: “What did this people do to you,” Moses asked Aaron, “that you have led them into so great a sin?”
bsb.32:22: “Do not be enraged, my lord,” Aaron replied. “You yourself know that the people are intent on evil.
bsb.32:23: They told me, ‘Make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him!’
bsb.32:24: So I said to them, ‘Whoever has gold, let him take it off,’ and they gave it to me. And when I threw it into the fire, out came this calf!”
bsb.32:25: Moses saw that the people were out of control, for Aaron had let them run wild and become a laughingstock to their enemies.
bsb.32:26: So Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and said, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me.” And all the Levites gathered around him.
bsb.32:27: He told them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Each of you men is to fasten his sword to his side, go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate, and slay his brother, his friend, and his neighbor.’”
bsb.32:28: The Levites did as Moses commanded, and that day about three thousand of the people fell dead.
bsb.32:29: Afterward, Moses said, “Today you have been ordained for service to the LORD, since each man went against his son and his brother; so the LORD has bestowed a blessing on you this day.”
bsb.32:30: The next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”
bsb.32:31: So Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Oh, what a great sin these people have committed! They have made gods of gold for themselves.
bsb.32:32: Yet now, if You would only forgive their sin.... But if not, please blot me out of the book that You have written.”
bsb.32:33: The LORD replied to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot out of My book.
bsb.32:34: Now go, lead the people to the place I described. Behold, My angel shall go before you. But on the day I settle accounts, I will punish them for their sin.”
bsb.32:35: And the LORD sent a plague on the people because of what they had done with the calf that Aaron had made.
bsb.33:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Leave this place, you and the people you brought up out of the land of Egypt, and go to the land that I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I said, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’
bsb.33:2: And I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
bsb.33:3: Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people; otherwise, I might destroy you on the way.”
bsb.33:4: When the people heard these bad tidings, they went into mourning, and no one put on any of his jewelry.
bsb.33:5: For the LORD had said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I should go with you for a single moment, I would destroy you. Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.’”
bsb.33:6: So the Israelites stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.
bsb.33:7: Now Moses used to take the tent and pitch it at a distance outside the camp. He called it the Tent of Meeting, and anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.
bsb.33:8: Then, whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would stand at the entrances to their own tents and watch Moses until he entered the tent.
bsb.33:9: As Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.
bsb.33:10: When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they would stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.
bsb.33:11: Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.
bsb.33:12: Then Moses said to the LORD, “Look, You have been telling me, ‘Lead this people up,’ but You have not let me know whom You will send with me. Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have found favor in My sight.’
bsb.33:13: Now if indeed I have found favor in Your sight, please let me know Your ways, that I may know You and find favor in Your sight. Remember that this nation is Your people.”
bsb.33:14: And the LORD answered, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
bsb.33:15: “If Your Presence does not go with us,” Moses replied, “do not lead us up from here.
bsb.33:16: For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us? How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?”
bsb.33:17: So the LORD said to Moses, “I will do this very thing you have asked, for you have found favor in My sight, and I know you by name.”
bsb.33:18: Then Moses said, “Please show me Your glory.”
bsb.33:19: “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you,” the LORD replied, “and I will proclaim My name—the LORD—in your presence. I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”
bsb.33:20: But He added, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.”
bsb.33:21: The LORD continued, “There is a place near Me where you are to stand upon a rock,
bsb.33:22: and when My glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.
bsb.33:23: Then I will take My hand away, and you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.”
bsb.34:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the originals, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
bsb.34:2: Be ready in the morning, and come up on Mount Sinai to present yourself before Me on the mountaintop.
bsb.34:3: No one may go up with you; in fact, no one may be seen anywhere on the mountain—not even the flocks or herds may graze in front of the mountain.”
bsb.34:4: So Moses chiseled out two stone tablets like the originals. He rose early in the morning, and taking the two stone tablets in his hands, he went up Mount Sinai as the LORD had commanded him.
bsb.34:5: And the LORD descended in a cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed His name, the LORD.
bsb.34:6: Then the LORD passed in front of Moses and called out: “The LORD, the LORD God, is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness,
bsb.34:7: maintaining loving devotion to a thousand generations, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin. Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished; He will visit the iniquity of the fathers on their children and grandchildren to the third and fourth generations.”
bsb.34:8: Moses immediately bowed down to the ground and worshiped.
bsb.34:9: “O Lord,” he said, “if I have indeed found favor in Your sight, my Lord, please go with us. Although this is a stiff-necked people, forgive our iniquity and sin, and take us as Your inheritance.”
bsb.34:10: And the LORD said, “Behold, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will perform wonders that have never been done in any nation in all the world. All the people among whom you live will see the LORD’s work, for it is an awesome thing that I am doing with you.
bsb.34:11: Observe what I command you this day. I will drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
bsb.34:12: Be careful not to make a treaty with the inhabitants of the land you are entering, lest they become a snare in your midst.
bsb.34:13: Rather, you must tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and chop down their Asherah poles.
bsb.34:14: For you must not worship any other god, for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
bsb.34:15: Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, for when they prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to them, they will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices.
bsb.34:16: And when you take some of their daughters as brides for your sons, their daughters will prostitute themselves to their gods and cause your sons to do the same.
bsb.34:17: You shall make no molten gods for yourselves.
bsb.34:18: You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. For seven days at the appointed time in the month of Abib, you are to eat unleavened bread as I commanded you. For in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
bsb.34:19: The first offspring of every womb belongs to Me, including all the firstborn males among your livestock, whether cattle or sheep.
bsb.34:20: You must redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb; but if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. You must redeem all the firstborn of your sons. No one shall appear before Me empty-handed.
bsb.34:21: Six days you shall labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest; even in the seasons of plowing and harvesting, you must rest.
